jobs.title: R&D Engineering Intern
jobs.body: Primary Responsibility: Summer 2027 Start Date: Sophomore - $22.15, Junior - $24.92, Senior - $27.69 The R&D Engineering Intern will work under the guidance of the engineering team and is responsible for design and development of innovative solutions for the Switching Devices product line. This position will contribute to the overall success of the product line with involvement in PRELaunch project research through manufacturing launch, participating in technology developments within the innovation pipeline, and leading sustainability projects. Functional responsibility includes design, testing and certification of switching devices assemblies and components with respect to performance, reliability, DFMA, and cost optimization of the final product. This position will work closely with the Engineering Manager, Program Manager, Engineering and MOL Supervisors, Design Engineers, Product Line Marketing Manager, Operations team members, Supply Chain Management and Manufacturing personnel in order to develop products per our Pro-Launch process. What you’ll do: ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: • Perform CAD solid modeling, design simulation, product specifications, drawing packages, Bill of Material (BOM) and Change Order (CO) creation, systems development, product testing and design validation • Design parts and assemblies which include component types including: sheet metal, plastics, mechanisms, electrical and wiring, and/or packaging • Participate in new product development/introduction, innovation, idea creation and implementation, prototype assembly and testing, DFMA assessments, plus other design-to-industrialization activities • Participate in project management and engaging with multi-disciplined teams to achieve goals using PROLaunch and other project management tools • Participate in Voice of the Customer (VOC) product and market requirements research • Maintain and upgrade existing products through MOL (Maintenance of Line) plus VAVE activity support • Provide assistance with 3rd party certifications such as UL, CSA, ISTA, and other regulatory agencies • Ensure timely completion to project commitment dates • Perform all operations using the highest safety and hygiene standards, electrical practices and established procedures. Maintain a clean, orderly, and safe workplace. • Work from written or verbal information, sketches, and drawings to perform design tests necessary to prove engineering designs, modifications, and improvements. • Assist technical personnel in recommending changes pertaining to dimensions, fits, tolerances, finishes, configuration, material and processes of parts and assemblies to enhance the possibility for design to pass design tests. • Assist in preparing equipment for design tests – support the equipment, making electrical connections to the test equipment, attaching thermal couples, applying insulation techniques, etc. • Complete test reports and all data entry using a computer, printer, photographs. • Assist witness tests forUL, CSA, and other certifying organizations. • Analyze design test results, such as temperature rise data, and make structure change recommendations to improve test results, if necessary. • Work with engineering sketches and oral instructions and/or engineering to set-up and perform design tests. • Provide prompt responses to design test requests to support production and customer ship dates. • Identify special or unusual conditions of design test failure modes, recommend design fixes to engineering, and assist engineering in developmental work. • Become familiar with all industry standards (IEEE, ANSI, NEMA, IEC, UL, & CSA) as necessary, to perform required equipment design tests. • Required travel to high power labs, like Belmont Labs, Belmont, NC or KEMA Labs, Chalfont, PA to assist engineering perform design tests • Obtains all necessary information to perform job assignment from engineers and manager. Works with little supervision to act as the primary contact for coordination of improvements. • Researches, analyzes, and helps specify purchases and equipment required for Design Lab projects with assistance from the engineers and manager. • Under direction from Engineers, modify or create technical drawings, material specs, work instructions, and relevant safety documentation. Qualifications: Basic Qualifications: • Must be pursuing a bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, or Engineering Technology from an accredited institution • Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc. • Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.8 or higher • Must be willing to relocate to the Cleveland, TN site for the internship. Relocation assistance will be provided for candidates that reside outside a 50-mile radius of Cleveland, TN. Preferred Qualifications: • Minimum of one internship or co-op experience or an equivalent of 3 months of relevant experience completed at the time of this application. Skills: • Understanding of phase gate project management tools and techniques • Experience working in a global business environment and with remote teams • Knowledge of ERP systems • Voice of the Customer (VOC) experience • Solid modeling experience and the ability to develop detailed 2D drawings with tolerance controls plus management of engineering documents via Change Order process • Experience performing various engineering tests and analyzing results • Contribute to team-driven product development projects with high level of personal accountability, and excellent communication skills • Adherence to Zero Incident Safety culture and processes

jobs.title: 2027 Mechanical Design Intern - Gilbert AZ
jobs.body: RELOCATION ASSISTANCE: Relocation assistance may be available CLEARANCE REQUIRED FOR START: No CLEARANCE TYPE: None TRAVEL: Yes, 10% of the Time Description At Northrop Grumman, our employees have incredible opportunities to work on revolutionary systems that impact people's lives around the world today, and for generations to come. Our pioneering and inventive spirit has enabled us to be at the forefront of many technological advancements in our nation's history - from the first flight across the Atlantic Ocean, to stealth bombers, to landing on the moon. We look for people who have bold new ideas, courage and a pioneering spirit to join forces to invent the future, and have fun along the way. Our culture thrives on intellectual curiosity, cognitive diversity and bringing your whole self to work — and we have an insatiable drive to do what others think is impossible. Our employees are not only part of history, they're making history. Northrop Grumman is a space pioneer, supporting government, civil and commercial customers in solving their biggest challenges. Our forward-leaning, innovative spirit is backed by a legacy of expertise that began at the dawn of the space age. Our mission experience in space runs deep, we know our customers well, and our capabilities are unmatched. This is what allows us to provide reliable, agile and affordable space solutions to best serve our customers. From defending freedom to advancing human discovery, we are defining what is possible in space every day. An internship at Northrop Grumman is unique. Sure, you’ll learn new skills, explore our enterprise, network with experts, connect with thought leaders, and finish with a resume that opens doors. But you’ll gain something even more valuable: pride in what you’ve done. Join us and launch your career. We’ll support you with training, professional development and networking opportunities, and our shared vision of global security. Northrop Grumman is seeking Mechanical Designers for an internship opportunity. This position will be located at our Space sector in Gilbert, AZ . The qualified candidate will become part of Northrop Grumman’s Gilbert Mechanical Engineering Department (Structure Design). Roles and Responsibilities Build 3D CAD models and generate engineering drawings to support satellite structure component design and procurement Interface with mechanical leads and cross disciplinary teams to understand subsystem design requirements Update engineering drawings in support of procurement, integration, and test activities Participate in/lead structure design group continuous improvement and training efforts Organize and archive structure design group technical data and documentation Basic Qualifications A candidate must meet ALL of the below criteria. The candidate must: Be a student who is enrolled full-time and pursuing an undergraduate or graduate degree from an accredited college/university and will be enrolled full time in Fall 2027 Be majoring in Mechanical Engineering or Aerospace Engineering Be available to work full-time (40 hours per week) for at least 10 weeks during summer 2027. Be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Government security clearance (U.S. citizenship is a pre-requisite) as well as Program Special access within a reasonable period of time, as determined by the company to meet its business needs (U.S. citizenship is a pre-requisite) Some mechanical design, mechanics of materials, and manufacturing coursework completed Knowledge of Creo or other CAD software Experience and success working within teams Proven ability to multi-task and self-starter able to work independently Strong interpersonal skills to drive actions necessary to accomplish assigned tasks Strong organizational skills in managing time, projects and resources Technical attention to detail on past projects and assignments Proficient in Microsoft Office tools including Word, Excel, PowerPoint Preferred Qualifications: Have an overall cumulative GPA of 3.00/4.0 or higher Experience with 3D printing or machining Proven leadership ability from past experiences• Ability to obtain and maintain a US Government Clearance Intern Pay Range: Bachelor’s: $18.50 to $33.50 per hour Master’s: $26.25 to $41.50 per hour At Northrop Grumman, our internship pay rates are standardized and take into account three main factors: the anticipated graduation date of the individual, the cost of labor of the geographic location, and whether the internship is considered technical or administrative. campusjobs The application period for the job is estimated to be 20 days from the job posting date. However, this timeline may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering NPD Intern
jobs.body: Badger Meter - Where Every Drop Counts and So Do You At Badger Meter, we're more than a leading global water technology company - we're innovators with a mission: to preserve and protect the world's most precious resource. For over 120 years, our trusted solutions have enabled our customers to optimize the delivery and use of water, maximize revenue and reduce waste. Every employee at Badger Meter is an important part of our success. Here, your work doesn't just move a business forward - it shapes a more sustainable future. We are committed to building a workplace where we celebrate differences, empower voices, and encourage fresh ideas that drive innovation. When you join us, you'll find: Purpose-driven work that makes a real difference in communities around the globe. Career growth and development opportunities designed to help you achieve your potential. A supportive, inclusive culture where collaboration and creativity thrive. Be part of something bigger. At Badger Meter, your contributions will ripple far beyond the workplace - creating lasting change for people and the planet. What You Will Contribute: The Badger Meter Internship Program provides hands-on, real-world experience to students through projects that make a difference! In addition to your projects, you will be given the opportunity to participate in our robust Intern program focused on Badger Meter Culture, professional development, community outreach, and a final capstone project. Badger Meter is hiring a Mechanical Engineering NPD Intern who will gain experience through new product development projects. This will be an onsite internship at our Milwaukee facility in summer 2027 (40 hours a week). What You Will Gain: Experience designing and developing mechanical components for new products. Hands-on experience testing and validating component and product performance. Exposure to creating and executing engineering test plans. Experience managing project deliverables and supporting New Product Development programs. Development of project management and program execution skills. Opportunities to present technical concepts, test results, and recommendations. Insight into the full product development lifecycle, from concept through launch. Preparation to contribute as an effective mechanical engineer in a fast-paced product development environment. ESSENTIAL JOB DUTIES: Support one or more New Product Development (NPD) projects within the Utility Mechanical Engineering team. Assist with development activities for next-generation ultrasonic meter platform products. Conduct engineering tests and document results. Design and develop test fixtures and testing methods. Perform engineering calculations, data analysis, and technical evaluations. Support prototype and product build events. Participate in design reviews and cross-functional engineering discussions. Collaborate with engineers to evaluate and improve product designs and performance. QUALIFICATIONS: Pursuing a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering. Progressing through core Mechanical Engineering coursework, including past completion of statics and dynamics. Currently studying machine elements, thermodynamics, and fluid mechanics. jobs.body: About the Team DoorDash Labs, established in 2018, serves as the innovation hub for DoorDash, focusing on developing automation and robotics solutions to enhance last-mile logistics. jobs.title: Product Development Engineering Co-op - Fall 2027
jobs.body: What you'll do: Fall 2027 Start Date: Sophomore - $22.15, Junior - $24.92, Senior - $27.69 PRIMARY RESPONSIBILITY: The Product Development Engineering Co-op will work under the guidance of the engineering team and is responsible for design and development of innovative solutions for the Busway product line. This position will contribute to the overall success of the product line with involvement in pre-launch project research through manufacturing launch as well as participating in technology developments within the innovation pipeline for both Pow-R-Way III and Powerwave 2 busway. Functional responsibility includes design, testing and certification of busway and busplug assemblies with respect to performance, reliability, DFMA, and cost optimization of the final product. This position will work closely with the Engineering Manager, Program Manager, Engineering and MOL Supervisors, Mechanical Engineers, Product Line Marketing Manager, Operations team members, Supply Chain Management and Manufacturing personnel in order to develop products per our Pro-Launch process. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS: Perform CAD solid modeling, design simulation, product specifications, drawing packages, Bill of Material (BOM) and Engineering Change Order (ECO) creation, systems development, product testing and design validation Design parts and assemblies which include component types including: sheet metal, plastics, mechanisms, electrical and wiring, and/or packaging Participate in new product development/introduction, innovation, idea creation and implementation, prototype assembly and testing, DFMA assessments, plus other design-to-industrialization activities Participate in project management and engaging with multi-disciplined teams to achieve goals using ProLaunch and other project management tools Participate in Voice of the Customer (VOC) product and market requirements research Maintain and upgrade existing products through MOL (Maintenance of Line) plus VAVE activity support Provide assistance with 3rd party certifications such as UL, CSA, ISTA, and other regulatory agencies Ensure timely completion to project commitment dates Perform all operations using the highest safety and hygiene standards, electrical practices and established procedures. Maintain a clean, orderly, and safe workplace. Work from written or verbal information, sketches, and drawings to perform design tests necessary to prove engineering designs, modifications, and improvements. What you’ll do: Assist technical personnel in recommending changes pertaining to dimensions, fits, tolerances, finishes, configuration, material and processes of parts and assemblies to enhance the possibility for design to pass design tests. Using basic mathematical principles make necessary mathematical computations and mechanical setups involved in the process of running electrical design tests. Understand and demonstrate knowledge of test equipment at on-site lab - impulse generator, current generator, Hi-pot box, environmental chamber along with oscilloscopes, oscillograms, camera, and digital camera Assist in preparing equipment for design tests – support the equipment, making electrical connections to the test equipment, attaching thermal couples, applying insulation techniques, etc. Complete test reports and all data entry using a computer, printer, photographs. Assist witness tests for ETL, UL, CSA, and other certifying organizations. Conduct required tests and calibration using design test equipment described above under the direction of technical personnel. Analyze design test results, such as temperature rise data, and make structure change recommendations to improve test results, if necessary. Work with engineering sketches and oral instructions and/or engineering to set-up and perform design tests. Provide prompt responses to design test requests to support production and customer ship dates. Identify special or unusual conditions of design test failure modes, recommend design fixes to engineering, and assist engineering in developmental work. Become familiar with all industry standards (IEEE, ANSI, NEMA, IEC, UL, & CSA) as necessary, to perform required equipment design tests. Required travel to high power labs, like Belmont Labs, Belmont, NC or KEMA Labs, Chalfont, PA to assist engineering perform design tests, such as short circuit current and are resistant tests. Obtains all necessary information to perform job assignment from Engineers and manager. Works with little supervision to act as the primary contact for coordination of improvements. Researches, analyzes, and helps specify purchases and equipment required for Design Lab projects with assistance from the Manufacturing and Maintenance of Line Engineers. Under direction from Engineers, modify or create technical drawings, material specs, work instructions, and relevant safety documentation. Qualifications: Basic Qualifications: Must be pursuing a bachelor's degree or master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, Electrical Engineering, or Engineering Technology from an accredited institution Eaton will not consider applicants for employment immigration sponsorship or support for this position. This means that Eaton will not support any CPT, OPT, or STEM OPT plans, F-1 to H-1B, H-1B cap registration, O-1, E-3, TN status, I-485 job portability, etc. Minimum cumulative GPA of 2.8 or higher (please don't round) Must be willing to relocate to the Hodges, SC site for the co-op. Relocation assistance will be provided for candidates that reside outside a 50-mile radius of Hodges, SC Skills: Understanding of phase gate project management tools and techniques Experience working in a global business environment and with remote teams Knowledge using ERP systems Voice of the Customer (VOC) experience CAD/SolidWorks/Inventor solid modeling experience and the ability to develop detailed 2D drawings with tolerance controls plus management of engineering documents via Engineering Change Order process Experience performing various engineering tests and analyzing results Contribute to team-driven product development projects with high level of personal accountability, and excellent communication skills Adherence to Zero Incident Safety culture and processes

jobs.title: Hardware Design Engineer Intern
jobs.body: Do you want to design the physical hardware that measures and controls the world’s most critical industrial processes? Emerson’s Process Systems and Solutions business develops automation products that power the energy and manufacturing industries. We are seeking a Hardware Design Intern (Summer 2027) who is passionate about electrical and mechanical engineering and excited to gain hands-on experience in a collaborative, innovative environment based in either our Round Rock, TX or Austin, TX office. You will join one of our hardware design teams that build the controllers, I/O, and field devices behind DeltaV , our flagship distributed process control system used by leading chemical, life sciences, and energy companies around the world. Working alongside experienced engineers and mentors, you will take on a summer project drawn from our real backlog. Potential project opportunities include PCB schematic capture, component placement, and board layout , FPGA design and verification, circuit simulation and analysis, or mechanical design work such as enclosures, thermal management, and manufacturability improvements. No prior industrial automation experience is required. If you enjoy designing and building things and want to see your work become hardware installed in plants around the world, we will teach you the rest. Many of our engineers joined us straight out of school from a general electrical or mechanical engineering background, and this internship is designed to be a great first exposure to professional product design. In This Role, Your Responsibilities Will Include: Partner with electrical and mechanical engineers and your mentor on a summer project that contributes to the hardware behind DeltaV controllers, I/O, and field devices. Contribute to schematic capture, component placement, and PCB layout, from initial concept through a design ready to be built. Support mechanical design work such as enclosures, mounting, and thermal management, and help evaluate designs for manufacturability. Use simulation and analysis tools to evaluate circuit, thermal, or mechanical performance before hardware is built. Work hands-on in the lab to bring up, measure, and troubleshoot prototype hardware using standard test equipment. Participate in design reviews and testing, and learn how professional teams take a product from concept to release. Take part in agile ceremonies such as sprint planning and retrospectives, along with Hackathons, Tech Talks, and Communities of Practice. Document what you build so the team can maintain and extend your work after your internship ends, and present your results to the team at the end of the summer. Who You Are: You are curious about how products are designed and built, and you enjoy the challenge of turning requirements into a real, physical design. You like solving problems and can break them down into manageable pieces. You are methodical when tracking down an unexpected measurement and comfortable being hands-on in the lab. You ask questions when something is unfamiliar, communicate effectively, and thrive in a team-oriented environment where electrical, mechanical, and software engineers work side by side. You take pride in your work and are motivated by seeing what you design become hardware customers rely on every day. For This Role, You Will Need: Currently enrolled in an accredited college/university and returning to school following the internship. Pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field. Coursework or project experience with CAD tools, whether electrical (schematic capture and PCB layout) or mechanical (3D modeling). Legal authorization to work in the United States. Sponsorship will not be provided for this position. Preferred Qualifications that Set You Apart: Junior or Senior standing. Experience with schematic capture and PCB layout tools such as Altium Designer, Cadence OrCAD or Allegro, Mentor/Siemens Xpedition, or KiCad. Experience with mechanical CAD tools such as SolidWorks, Creo, NX, or AutoCAD. Familiarity with circuit simulation and analysis tools such as SPICE, or with thermal and structural simulation. Exposure to digital and analog circuit design fundamentals, including power supply design and component selection. Exposure to FPGA design and verification using an HDL such as VHDL or Verilog. Understanding of signal integrity, power distribution, grounding, or thermal management considerations in board design. Interest in design for manufacturability, enclosure design, or materials selection. Awareness of agency and compliance requirements such as UL, EMC, hazardous location, or intrinsic safety. Comfort with hands-on lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, multimeters, power supplies, and logic analyzers. Coursework or project experience in a programming or scripting language such as Python, C, C++, or MATLAB. Interest in applying AI/ML techniques to hardware design, simulation, or test problems. Previous internship, class project, hackathon, or personal project experience in hardware design. Our Culture & Commitment to You:​ At Emerson, we prioritize a workplace where every employee is valued, respected, and empowered to grow. We foster an environment that encourages innovation, collaboration, and diverse perspectives because we know that great ideas come from great teams. Our commitment to ongoing career development and growing an inclusive culture ensures you have the support to thrive. Whether through mentorship, training, or leadership opportunities, we invest in your success so you can make a lasting impact. We believe diverse teams working together are key to driving growth and delivering business results. ​ What You’ll Gain: Real-world experience contributing work that ships as part of a product used in plants around the world. Direct mentorship from experienced engineers and a close look at how professional teams design, build, test, and release products. Practical, resume-ready skills in PCB design, mechanical design, and hands-on hardware bring-up and test.

jobs.title: Test Engineer Intern, ESS (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Peak Energy Role Title : Test Engineer Intern Location: Burlingame, CA Department: Engineering Reports To: Senior Manager, Test Engineering Position Type: Internship (Summer 2027) About Peak Energy Peak Energy is the first American venture to advance globally proven Sodium-Ion battery systems as the storage standard for the new era of renewable energy on a resilient grid. Sodium-Ion is cheap, readily available and safe, making it the leading contender in a rapidly evolving market. Our leadership team is powered by decades of expertise in scaling gigawatt-level innovation at world-class companies such as Tesla, Northvolt, Apple, Powin, Enovix, Zipline, Solid Power, and Fluence. We are backed by strategic investment and product partners such as TDK Ventures and Eclipse Ventures. We are a team of engineers, operators, entrepreneurs, and partners driven by a shared ambition to set the new performance standard for renewable energy and grid resilience. About the Role – Test Engineer Intern We are looking for a Test Engineer Intern to support our testing and functional verification efforts for our energy storage systems, from battery to power electronics. This role will work closely with design and simulation teams to understand needs, develop procedures, set up and run tests, and report on findings that directly inform the design direction of our products. You will interface with design, simulation, and manufacturing engineering partners and gain hands-on experience across a fast-moving, early-stage energy company. Candidates should be available to begin employment in Summer 2027. The ideal candidate is a self-starter who is hungry for knowledge, holds themselves and others to high standards, and brings a get-it-done attitude to every challenge — big or small. What You'll Do Conduct comprehensive testing of functional, high voltage, thermal, and mechanical systems across our energy storage products Develop test strategies, plans, and procedures to evaluate key risks Spearhead the design and acquisition of testing infrastructure Collaborate with engineering teams to ensure design integrity and drive improvements Analyze complex test data, report findings, and drive system enhancements Identify, diagnose, and resolve intricate technical issues during testing Perform root cause analysis on system failures and develop corrective and preventive actions Drive innovation in testing methodologies and practices Interface tightly with design, simulation, and manufacturing engineering partners to inform design decisions Maintain detailed records of tests, analyses, and corrective actions; prepare reports and presentations for internal and external stakeholders Drive and participate in a culture of rapid prototyping and automation What You'll Bring Working towards a Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field Experience in test engineering, preferably within battery storage or renewable energy sectors Strong understanding of electromechanical engineering first principles Proficiency in data processing and analysis tools Excellent problem-solving skills with the ability to think critically and act decisively Strong communication skills with the ability to present complex technical information clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders Ability to work collaboratively in a fast-paced, dynamic environment Proactive ownership mindset with a strong sense of accountability Preferred Qualifications Experience with battery systems, energy storage, or power electronics testing Familiarity with automated test systems or rapid prototyping workflows Background in reliability, abuse, or environmental stress testing Peak Energy is committed to building a diverse and inclusive workforce. jobs.title: Process Engineering Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. ABOUT THE ROLE: We are seeking a motivated and hands-on Process Engineering Intern to support the development, implementation, and continuous improvement of manufacturing processes for our current and next generation of autonomous products. In this role, you will work alongside experienced engineers to improve production efficiency, optimize manufacturing processes, and support new product introductions. Your contributions will help drive quality, productivity, and operational scalability across our manufacturing operations. HOW YOU'LL MAKE AN IMPACT: - Support the development and continuous improvement of manufacturing processes to improve production efficiency, quality, and operator ergonomics. - Conduct time studies and analyze manufacturing cycle times to identify bottlenecks, reduce waste, and improve labor efficiency. - Assist in developing and maintaining standard work instructions, process documentation, and visual manufacturing aids. - Support production capacity studies, line balancing, and labor modeling to identify opportunities for throughput improvements. - Collaborate with Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Production, and Supply Chain teams to support new product introductions (NPI) and production ramp activities. - Analyze production performance data, including cycle times, downtime, and Overall Equipment Effectiveness (OEE), to identify improvement opportunities. - Assist with production line layouts, workstation design, and material flow improvements to optimize space utilization and manufacturing efficiency. - Participate in Lean Manufacturing and continuous improvement initiatives, including root cause analysis, waste reduction, and process standardization. - Support engineering projects from planning through implementation, including data collection, process trials, and validation of improvements. - Work directly with production operators and technicians to troubleshoot manufacturing challenges and implement practical solutions. WHAT MAKES YOU A GOOD FIT: - Currently pursuing a bachelor's or master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field. - Basic understanding of manufacturing processes, industrial engineering principles, and continuous improvement methodologies. - Familiarity with time study techniques, predetermined motion time systems such as MOST or MODAPTS, or work measurement principles is a plus. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to collect, organize, and interpret data. - Proficiency with Microsoft Excel or similar data analysis tools; experience with Python, SQL, or Power BI is a plus. - Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing concepts, standard work, line balancing, or capacity analysis is a plus. - Experience with CAD software such as AutoCAD, Fusion 360, or SolidWorks is a plus. - Strong organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks and projects in a fast-paced environment. - Excellent communication and teamwork skills with an eagerness to learn from engineers, technicians, and production operators. - Enthusiasm for hands-on engineering, manufacturing operations, and developing creative solutions to real-world challenges. Compensation Range: The hourly base salary range for this position is $47/hr for Undergrad, $53/hr for Graduate students, and $70/hr for PhD students*. Compensation will vary based on factors, including skill level, proficiencies, transferable knowledge, and experience. *For some positions the pay may be dependent upon the individual's regional location. #LI-ZD1 At Skydio we believe that diversity drives innovation. We have created a multidisciplinary environment that embraces the power of diverse perspectives to create elegant solutions for complex problems. We are committed to growing our network of people, programs, and resources to nurture an inclusive culture. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, or other characteristics protected by federal, state or local anti-discrimination laws. jobs.title: Ground Systems Engineering Intern Summer 2027
jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As a Grounds Systems Engineering Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Stennis, Mississippi, you will have the opportunity to support the Test Ground Systems team as they provide the Archimedes engine with everything it needs to see for test, and provide the instrumentation, controls, and automation necessary to capture any and all data to accelerate the Neutron Program. The Ground Systems team is an integral part of the testing team, from designing and building new stands and capabilities, to making sure the stand continues to run smoothly day to day every day offers new challenges and opportunities to grow and contribute to the success of the mission. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering discipline such as Electrical, Mechatronics or Robotics Engineering, or physics discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Experience with Solidworks and MATLAB Finite Element Analysis (FEA) experience Computer-aided design and manufacturing (CAD/ CAM) experience Lathe Machining experience Geometric Dimensioning & Tolerancing experience Python and C++ experience Experience working with pressurized systems Proficient knowledge of fluid dynamics ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. We thrive under pressure, work to tight deadlines, and our focus is always on how we can deliver, rather than dwelling on the challenges that stand in the way. jobs.title: Thermofluids Analysis Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: About Us At Antares, our long-term mission is to make clean energy abundant from Earth to the Asteroid Belt. We’re fueled by the belief that advanced nuclear energy can strengthen our military, solve the climate crisis, elevate global living standards, and expand humanity's presence in outer space. To achieve our mission, we’re building mass-producible, inherently safe, deployable microreactors that can be used terrestrially, underwater, and in space. The Antares team hails from SpaceX, the White House, the Pentagon, the Department of Energy, MIT, Rigetti Computing, General Atomics, Relativity Space, Ursa Major, and National Laboratories like Idaho, Oak Ridge, Los Alamos, and Savannah River. Antares has raised over $600M in venture capital from top-tier investors and has hundreds of million-dollars on contract with the military services, NASA, and the Department of Energy. About the Summer Internship Program Internships at Antares are anything but ordinary. You'll work alongside our team as we design, build, and test fission microreactors built to deliver reliable energy for critical missions on Earth, in space, and underwater. Our interns contribute to real work from day one. Depending on your role, you may touch hardware, write and test software, support manufacturing and operations, or help build the systems that allow Antares to move quickly as we scale. You'll work alongside engineers, operators, and other experts solving challenging problems—and you'll leave your internship with hands-on experience that's difficult to find anywhere else. We work hard, move quickly, and take pride in what we're building. If you're excited to learn by doing and want to contribute to the next generation of nuclear energy, we'd love to have you join us next summer. We will be running two separate cohorts to accommodate students on both semester and quarter schedules: Cohort #1 Monday, May 17 – Friday, August 13 Cohort #2 Monday, June 14 – Friday, September 10 All internship roles are based at our Torrance headquarters and require interns to work onsite five days per week. We will not be considering candidates for remote or hybrid arrangements. Interns will receive a relocation and housing stipend as part of their offer package. About the Team The Analysis team at Antares develops and applies physics-based models to guide the design, testing, and development of reactor systems. The team works across engineering disciplines to size components, understand thermal and fluid performance, evaluate structural response, and turn simulation and test data into engineering decisions. Interns begin with small starter projects and then quickly take ownership of a long-duration project that culminates in a technical deliverable and presentation. You will be integrated and evaluated as if you are a first-year junior engineer, not simply an intern. The bar for success is high: you will be expected to use your mentor and the resources around you thoughtfully, execute on your project, and identify additional issues and opportunities for improvement. Roles and Responsibilities: - Build CFD models of reactor components to evaluate fluid flow, heat transfer, and component performance. - Build FEA models of reactor components to evaluate relevant thermal and structural behavior. - Develop Python tools that support the sizing and evaluation of new designs. - Process, review, and interpret test data; compare results with analytical and numerical predictions. - Define model assumptions, boundary conditions, and inputs, and assess convergence, sensitivity, and model fidelity. - Document methods, results, limitations, and recommendations in clear technical deliverables. - Complete initial starter projects, then own a long-duration project through final technical presentation. - Collaborate with mentors and cross-functional engineering partners while proactively identifying technical risks and opportunities for improvement. Basic Qualifications: - Currently enrolled in at least a bachelor's degree program in mechanical, aerospace, nuclear, chemical, or another relevant engineering discipline and entering the junior or senior year of study. - Prior internship experience or more than one year of significant project-team, laboratory, or research experience. Preferred Skills & Experience: - GPA of 3.5 or above. - Experience in a university club or organization; leadership experience is preferred. - Strong interpersonal and technical communication skills, such as leading a student project team or presenting research at a conference. - Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with close attention to detail. - Ability to work cross-functionally with different groups and teams. - Ability to work effectively in a dynamic environment with changing needs and requirements. - Ability to work independently and collaboratively, take initiative, and communicate effectively. - Experience with Python and engineering data analysis. - Experience with CFD, FEA, CAD, MATLAB, or related modeling and analysis tools. - Coursework or project experience in thermodynamics, fluid mechanics, heat transfer, numerical methods, or solid mechanics. Location - We are located in Torrance, CA in a 322,000 square foot, brand new facility featuring large open spaces for team collaboration, R&D, and production, as well as easy access to the 405, 105, and 110 freeways. Our facility is in the heart of Los Angeles' vibrant emerging tech ecosystem alongside many other high growth startups and enterprises. Culture At Antares, we like to specifically tie each role to our founding document’s set of values–here are the top five cultural values we think you should believe at your core to be successful: - Think in Systems - Energy and Defense are complex ecosystems with numerous stakeholders with competing priorities, conflicting policies, perverse incentives, and emergent and path-dependent properties. First principles thinking alone is insufficient. Think probabilistically and then take action. “If you want to be certain, then you are apt to be obsolete.” Over-optimizing the components often degrades the system - Obsess over the End User - The customer and end user are often not the same. We will never build globally competitive commercial products if we lose sight of our end users and their entire interaction with the product life cycle - Be Unconstrained by Convention - Our only limits are the laws of physics. Many, even experts, will say what we are working on is impossible. They said the same about SpaceX reusing rockets. Generationally impactful companies, by definition, must accomplish the seemingly impossible. If it were easy, it would have already been done. Never shy away from a solution because it has never been tried before, and never choose to do something because that's “how it's always been done” - Go Where the Work Is - Never miss a chance to meet a customer, user, or stakeholder face to face, even if that means hopping on a plane. If you can’t make it, find a teammate who can channel your intentions and go in your place. Deep work can be done from anywhere, but we believe teams are built in person, and aim to maximize our time together - Operate in the Grey - Embrace nuance in pursuit of truth. Question every fundamental assumption Equal Opportunity Antares is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Employment decisions are based solely on merit, competence, and qualifications, without regard to race, color, religion, gender, national origin/ethnicity, veteran status, disability status, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, marital status, mental or physical disability, or any other legally protected status. jobs.title: Silicon Validation Intern, BS - Summer 2027
jobs.body: About Marvell Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. Your Team, Your Impact The Rack Scale Switch Chip Validation team validates and delivers the high-performance switching silicon and system-level solutions used inside modern AI and cloud data center racks. As an intern, you will contribute to day-to-day engineering work such as running emulation and verification tests, debugging silicon and hardware issues, troubleshooting switch performance and efficiency, and writing scripts to automate workflows, all alongside experienced engineers. Your work will support the team's efforts to deliver reliable, high-bandwidth, low-latency switch products that are a key part of Marvell's data infrastructure portfolio. These products help customers scale AI workloads and enable the next generation of data center networking. What You Can Expect Support post-silicon validation of high-speed switch silicon under the guidance of senior engineers. · Assist in developing, documenting, and executing test plans and test cases for switch chip validation. · Support lab-based silicon bring-up and run unit tests on hardware and firmware functionality, including emulation and verification environments. · Help collect and analyze high-speed signal and link data (such as eye diagrams, jitter, and BER) using lab test equipment. · Assist in debugging silicon and hardware issues, and in troubleshooting switch performance and efficiency. · Use diagnostics, software tools, oscilloscopes, and protocol analyzers to help isolate the root cause of failing tests. · Write and maintain scripts (for example in Python) to automate test execution, data collection, and result reporting. · Document test results, findings, and debug progress, and present them to the team. What We're Looking For · Currently pursuing a bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028 · Foundational understanding of digital logic, computer architecture, and high-speed I/O concepts such as SerDes and PCIe or Ethernet protocols. · Basic hands-on lab experience through coursework, research, or projects, such as hardware bring-up, testing, and debug. · Familiarity with common lab equipment such as oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, or BERTs. · Programming or scripting experience in Python, Perl, or a similar language. · Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills, with a willingness to learn. Preferred/Plus: · Coursework or project experience with PCIe, Ethernet, or other high-speed interfaces. · Exposure to the physical and protocol layers of high-speed interfaces (for example PHY, PCS, MAC). · Experience with emulation, simulation, or verification environments. · Ability to read board schematics and layouts. · Familiarity with signal integrity concepts such as eye diagrams, jitter, and BER. jobs.title: Vehicle Integration & Test Internship - Summer 2027
jobs.body: About Varda Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses. From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind. Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital. Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL. Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem. About This Role Summer internships will range between the months of May and August. All dates dependent upon the university schedule of the selected students. jobs.title: System Test Automation Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the System Validation Team The System Validation Team ensures the performance, reliability, and safety of Zipline’s integrated system of systems, including the Zip, Droid, and Dock. We specialize in Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) testing, enabling us to validate complex interactions across hardware and software before real-world deployment. Our team builds and maintains automated pipelines that rigorously test software in a simulated environment, ensuring it meets high standards before being tested in flight. By catching potential issues early and refining system behavior, we play a critical role in delivering reliable, safe, and efficient solutions that power Zipline’s mission to transform global logistics. Our team owns automation of flight testing as well to capture issues before it happens in commercial flights. The Role As a System Validation Intern, you will contribute to testing and validating Zipline’s complete system of systems—spanning the Zip, Droid, and Dock. You’ll help build and refine automated testing pipelines, ensuring that software meets rigorous quality standards before being tested in flight. Working closely with a supportive and experienced team, you’ll develop hands-on experience with cutting-edge tools and technologies while solving meaningful challenges. Your work will play an essential role in ensuring the reliability of systems that deliver life-saving goods worldwide. This role offers a unique opportunity to learn, grow, and make an impact in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment. What You'll Do Assist in executing Hardware-in-the-Loop (HIL) tests and flight tests to validate the interaction between Zipline’s Zip, Droid, and Dock systems. Collaborate with a wide range of engineers from different teams to build and refine automated pipelines that test software before it is deployed in flight. Design and improve tools that stress-test the system in off-nominal cases. Analyze and troubleshoot hardware and software issues uncovered during testing, contributing to system improvements. Work alongside a multidisciplinary team to design and execute system-level validation plans. Develop and enhance scripts and tools to support automated testing workflows. Learn how to ensure reliability and quality in complex, safety-critical systems, gaining valuable insights into real-world engineering challenges. What You'll Bring You must have completed the second year of your undergraduate studies. Master's and PhD students are also eligible. Strong understanding of engineering design fundamentals and the ability to triage and identify root causes of technical issues. Experience writing Rust or Python scripts to automate tasks or tests, either through coursework or personal projects. Hands-on experience writing Python tests using tools like Pytest or Unittest. Familiarity with creating and executing test plans or validation plans for software or hardware systems. A hands-on approach to problem-solving, including debugging and triaging technical issues. General understanding of electrical systems such as motors, sensors, cameras, and onboard computers. Experience working in a Linux environment, including using command-line tools effectively. Familiarity with tools like Git for version control, bazel for build and test management and Jira for task tracking. Basic understanding of networking concepts such as RPC or sockets. Experience working with CI tools like GitHub Actions, Buildkite, or similar. Strong attention to detail and organizational skills to document test results and track issues effectively. What Else You Should Know This internship is a full-time position, in-person at our South San Francisco office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from (May/June - August/September). The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements. Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: Safety & Systems Engineering Intern
jobs.body: Who we are Aurora’s mission is to deliver the benefits of self-driving technology safely, quickly, and broadly. The Aurora Driver https://aurora.tech will create a new era in mobility and logistics, one that will bring a safer, more efficient, and more accessible future to everyone. At Aurora, you will tackle massively complex problems alongside other passionate, intelligent individuals, growing as an expert while expanding your knowledge. For the latest news from Aurora, visit aurora.tech http://aurora.tech or follow us on LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/company/auroradriver. What we are looking for We're searching for Summer 2027 Safety & Systems Engineering Interns. You'll work on the systems and safety engineering that holds a safety-critical driving product to its requirements — functional safety, behavioral and system safety, systems-engineering process, and requirements/fault analysis for the Aurora Driver. In this role you will - Perform safety analysis to identify root causes and common-cause failures across vehicle, system, or software subsystems - Build tooling to support safety-analysis or requirements-development processes - Analyze test coverage and data to determine whether the system meets its safety and behavioral requirements - Explore external and internal data sources to identify previously unknown scenarios or system sensitivities - Communicate findings and recommendations clearly to engineering stakeholders Required qualifications - Currently pursuing a Bachelor's, Master's or PhD in Systems Engineering, Automotive Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related field - Some exposure to a system where failure had real consequences, even at the coursework or club-project level - Familiarity with structured failure-analysis methods (FMEA, fault trees, STPA, or other formal root-cause methods) - Regular use of Python for analysis or tooling - Experience running an analysis as part of a trade study - Ability to reason about evidence and statistics — coverage and confidence, not just pass/fail counts Desirable qualifications - Prior safety-engineering experience (functional safety, ISO 26262-class standards) - C++ experience - Experience with UML/SysML Compensation The hourly pay rate for this internship in Mountain View is: - $58.00 per hour for interns pursuing a master’s degree; and - $65.00 per hour for interns pursuing a doctoral degree. The hourly pay rate for this internship in Pittsburgh is: - $52.00 per hour for interns pursuing a master’s degree; and - $58.00 per hour for interns pursuing a doctoral degree. Working at Aurora At Aurora, we bring together extraordinarily talented and experienced people united by the strength of our values. We operate with integrity, set outrageous goals, and build a culture where we win together — all without any jerks. We believe in-person work increases collaboration, empathy, and our ability to lead effectively. As a result, Aurorans are expected to work from the office at least 3 days per week, with some roles requiring more frequent in-office presence, up to 5 days per week, based on operational needs. Our Careers page https://aurora.tech/careers provides insight into what it is like to work at Aurora, and you can find all the latest updates in our Newsroom https://aurora.tech/newsroom. Our commitment to safety At the core of everything we do is our commitment to safety. Building best-in-class self-driving technology will take time, and we believe that each employee at Aurora has a role in contributing to safety, every step of the way. Aurora expects commitment to our safety policies from every employee, and seeks candidates who take an active responsibility, can contribute to building an atmosphere of trust, and invest in the organization’s long-term success by prioritizing working safely, no matter what. Our commitment to inclusion Aurora considers candidates without regard to their race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex, gender, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, marital status, pregnancy status, parent or caregiver status, ancestry, political affiliation, veteran and/or military status, physical or mental disability, or any other status protected by federal or state law. Aurora considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state, and local law. We are also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. jobs.title: Additive Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)

jobs.title: Environmental Test Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About the role Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules. Internship is full-time and on-site in San Jose, California. The Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) team at Muon is responsible for validating spacecraft hardware through unit acceptance testing as well as spacecraft-level integration and environmental testing. As an Environmental Test Engineering Intern, you will support the planning, setup, execution, and analysis of environmental tests used to validate spacecraft hardware against the extreme conditions of launch and space. You will work alongside experienced environmental test engineers, test engineers, and technicians to prepare hardware and test equipment, develop and execute test procedures, collect and analyze test data, and troubleshoot test issues. This is a hands-on opportunity to gain experience with spacecraft environmental testing and see your work directly contribute to the successful integration and launch of Muon spacecraft. Muon is a small and fast growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success. Responsibilities Assist environmental test engineers with the planning, preparation, and execution of spacecraft and subsystem environmental testing, including thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, and other qualification or acceptance testing. Support test setup and instrumentation, including thermocouples, accelerometers, pressure sensors, and other test measurement equipment. Assist with preparing spacecraft hardware, fixtures, ground support equipment, and test configurations for environmental test campaigns. Execute functional checkouts and test procedures under engineer supervision before, during, and after environmental testing. Monitor test operations and hardware performance, identify anomalies, and support troubleshooting and root-cause investigations. Collect, process, and perform preliminary analysis of environmental test data to verify hardware performance and test requirements. Support development and improvement of test procedures, test processes, checklists, and laboratory workflows. Assist with configuration and operation of environmental test equipment and data acquisition systems. Support automation and scripting efforts to improve environmental test setup, monitoring, data collection, and analysis. Generate test documentation, data summaries, and reports under the guidance of environmental test engineers. Support integration and handling of spacecraft hardware and ground support equipment in cleanroom, laboratory, and environmental test facilities. Help maintain a safe, organized, and flight-hardware-ready test environment. Qualifications Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Electrical, Systems Engineering, or a related technical field. Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals, particularly in areas such as mechanics, thermal systems, dynamics, instrumentation, or electrical systems. Demonstrated interest in spacecraft environmental testing, laboratory testing, or hardware development. Experience with a programming or scripting language for data analysis or test automation, such as Python, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, or C++. Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to approach complex technical challenges from a first-principles perspective. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment. Ability and willingness to work hands-on with engineering hardware and test equipment. Nice-to-have Skills Previous internship, co-op, research, or laboratory experience involving hardware testing. Experience with thermal vacuum, vibration, acoustic, shock, or other environmental testing. Experience with data acquisition systems, instrumentation, sensors, or test equipment. Experience developing test procedures, test plans, or test reports. Experience with accelerometers, thermocouples, pressure transducers, strain gauges, or similar instrumentation. Experience with Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW, or other tools used for test automation and data analysis. Previous experience on technical project teams such as a CubeSat, rocketry, Formula SAE, Solar Car, or other hardware-focused engineering project. Familiarity with spacecraft systems or subsystems and environmental test requirements. Experience with hardware integration, troubleshooting, or hardware-in-the-loop testing. Pay range Bachelor's students $40/hour Master's $45/hour PhD $50/hour About Muon Space Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world. Taking Care of Our Team At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave. Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too. Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. jobs.title: Wireless Hardware Engineer Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: Skydio is the leading US drone company and the world leader in autonomous flight, the key technology for the future of drones and aerial mobility. The Skydio team combines deep expertise in artificial intelligence, best-in-class hardware and software product development, operational excellence, and customer obsession to empower a broader, more diverse audience of drone users, from utility inspectors https://www.skydio.com/solutions/energy-and-utilities to first responders https://www.skydio.com/solutions/public-safety, soldiers in battlefield scenarios https://www.skydio.com/solutions/national-security/tactical-isr, and beyond https://www.skydio.com/solutions. About the role: We are looking for a highly motivated Summer Intern to support our Wireless Engineering team in design validation and data analysis. This role focuses on building scalable data processing pipelines and tools that enable efficient analysis of wireless validation data from both bench testing and factory testing environments. You will work closely with RF and antenna engineers to improve how wireless performance data is collected, processed, and visualized. You will help accelerate product development and manufacturing readiness. This is a great opportunity for someone who enjoys working at the intersection of wireless systems and cloud-based data engineering. How you'll make an impact (example projects below): - Develop automated data processing pipelines to analyze RF and antenna validation data from lab bench testing. - Build cloud-based tools and dashboards to streamline factory test data ingestion, processing, and visualization. - Improve data quality checks and validation frameworks to ensure reliable wireless performance metrics. - Partner with RF engineers to translate test requirements into scalable analysis workflows. - Optimize existing scripts and infrastructure to improve efficiency and reproducibility of wireless performance analysis. - Contribute to documentation and best practices for wireless data management across development and manufacturing. What makes you a good fit: - Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s (Upcoming junior or senior), Master’s, or PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related field. - Strong fundamentals in wireless systems, RF engineering, or antenna theory. - Proficiency in cloud-based development and data processing (e.g., Python, data pipelines, scripting, APIs). - Experience working with large datasets and building scalable analysis tools. - Familiarity with data visualization tools or frameworks is a plus. - Comfortable working in a cross-functional engineering environment. - Self-driven, detail-oriented, and eager to learn and contribute in a fast-paced setting. jobs.title: Summer 2027 - Validation Engineering Intern
jobs.body: onsemi (Nasdaq: ON) is driving disruptive innovations to help build a better future. With a focus on automotive and industrial end-markets, the company is accelerating change in megatrends such as vehicle electrification and safety, sustainable energy grids, industrial automation, and 5G and cloud infrastructure. With a highly differentiated and innovative product portfolio, onsemi creates intelligent power and sensing technologies that solve the world’s most complex challenges and leads the way in creating a safer, cleaner, and smarter world. Here at onsemi we take great pride in our internship program and the efforts we take to provide students with hands-on industry experience. We provide competitive pay, medical benefits, various networking event opportunities, and flexible hours based on school schedule. onsemi is seeking a highly skilled and motivated intern to join our Validation Engineering team to work cross functionally with technology development, design, quality assurance, product engineering, test, and applications engineering. Validation Engineering is responsible for planning and executing product validation activities that confirm sensor performance, functionality, reliability readiness, and manufacturability from early silicon through production release. With a strong focus on test development, data analysis, debug, and issue resolution, Validation Engineering plays a central role in validating new products, identifying risks, supporting silicon bring-up, and enabling high-quality customer and production readiness. The ideal candidate is excited by working cross-functionally on a diverse range of technical challenges with an eye to continuous learning and developing the competencies needed to find solutions. This opportunity will ask a student to have the following performance objectives: Support validation planning, silicon bring-up, debug, and characterization of new and derivative image sensor products, including test chips targeted at circuit and process learning, reliability readiness, and manufacturability. Validate new circuit IP and sensor functions such as memories, OTPM, pumps, regulators, serial communication interfaces, safety mechanisms, and new DFT test modes. Develop and improve validation test methodologies, automation, and data analysis flows to detect issues early, reduce debug cycle time, and support robust product release decisions. Enhance the performance and usability of existing validation tools by improving scripts, automation, documentation, and reporting workflows. Support failure analysis, root-cause investigation, and cross-functional debug activities as key components of the validation engineering role. In order to be considered for an internship, you must be a student currently enrolled in school pursuing an accredited degree program. This position is specifically looking for someone who is enrolled in a Bachelor’s, Master’s, or doctoral program in Electrical Engineering or related field with emphasis on chip level circuit design. Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering in progress, or related field with coursework on analog and digital circuit design. Solid understanding of semiconductor device physics. Proficient in scripting languages (e.g. Python, VB, Perl, C, bash). Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Strong team player and ability to work well in a collaborative environment. Experience with Electrical lab equipment (e.g. oscilloscopes, power supplies, power meters, signal generators). Familiarity with CMOS Circuit design and test methodology preferred. Understanding of imager sensor architecture and product reliability requirements preferred.
