jobs.title: Design Co-op Summer 2027
jobs.body: Job Location CINCINNATI GENERAL OFFICES Job Description P&G Design is a group of world-class design thinkers and practitioners across multiple design disciplines including graphic, industrial, innovation, digital, fashion and more. Whether it’s refreshing a brand identity, crafting a new 3D shape for an iconic brand, or designing a new app, design is at the heart of meeting the needs of today’s consumers. As a Design Co-op, you are responsible for crafting excellent design solutions that support the brand strategy and business objectives. All of our co-op roles will include hands-on design along with envisioning, and executing solutions for packaging, product and digital contexts. What roles are available? The Graphic Design Co-op role at P&G amplifies and executes the visual expression of a brand and how it comes to life across touchpoints (including packaging, in-store, digital/social, etc.). As a Co-op, you will partner with creative leaders, agency partners, and marketers to influence brand and design strategies and create extraordinary design solutions. You will work through all parts of the design process, assessing the landscape, brainstorming, and continuing through design and content creation. Creative thinking, project management, and collaboration with multi-functional teams are an important part of this role. We look for majors/degrees in Graphic Design, Fashion Design, or Textile Design for these roles. The Industrial Design Co-op role is a developer of package, device, and delivery systems ranging from ground-breaking innovations to reinventing key products. You will partner with engineers and technologists to deliver P&G’s innovation pipeline. You will work through the end-to-end design process, from brainstorming and ideation, deep consumer insight, to prototyping and execution. Creative thinking, project management and collaboration with multi-functional teams are an important part of this role. We look for majors/degrees in Industrial Design for these roles. The Innovation Design Engineer Co-Op role at P&G is a technical expert, partnering with Innovation Design teams to prototype and actualize concepts for superior consumer experiences. This involves developing novel product ideas, from mechanical to complex electro-mechanical devices. You'll influence stakeholders and suppliers throughout the product lifecycle, solving complex engineering challenges from early innovation to Design for Manufacture (DFM). You'll translate consumer needs into technical specifications, utilizing resources like The Innovation Shop and 2D/3D Printing Lab to create high-fidelity prototypes for class-leading products. The Digital Content Creator Co-op role at P&G amplifies and executes the visual expression of a brand and how it comes to life across all digital touchpoints, including social media, e-commerce platforms, websites, and digital advertising. As a Co-op, you will partner with creative leaders, agency partners, and marketers to influence brand and digital content strategies and create extraordinary online visual solutions. You will work through all parts of the content creation process, assessing the digital landscape, brainstorming concepts, and continuing through design and content production for various online platforms. Creative thinking, project management, and collaboration with multi-functional teams are an important part of this role. We look for majors/degrees in Graphic Design, Digital Media, Marketing with a digital focus, or related fields for these roles. The UX/UI Design Co-op role is a hybrid of communication design, UX/UI and content creation (both video and still). This position requires a diverse set of skills in order to help lean innovation teams move fast and learn efficiently. You will collaborate with Industrial Designers, Marketers, and Engineers to help push the story behind products and communicate to consumers. You will help take projects from brainstorm, to ideation, to execution, no matter the medium (web design, photography shoots, how to videos, Facebook ads, etc.) while keeping a strong graphic design aesthetic. We look for majors/degrees in UI/UX Design, Communication Design, Interactive Design, Digital Design, New Media Design, or Advertising Design. Job Qualifications We believe this is ideal for you if you are attending a university/college with a major in design and have a portfolio that demonstrates: Creative Excellence – aesthetics and visualization skills, visual storytelling, and creative resolution. Our early career programs are designed to attract inventive minds, offering a platform to contribute to our long-term innovation pipeline. You'll be part of a community that values collaboration, creativity, and continuous learning. As a QGOV Engineering Intern, you will sit in either San Diego, CA or Boulder, CO and support government-sponsored research, development, integration, and testing of such systems, including adaptation and extension of commercial systems to novel applications and environments, as well as internal development efforts. You will work on a variety of projects crossing multiple disciplines from across the company to deliver timely results to customers. You will be responsible for working closely with other engineering disciplines to design, develop, automate, document, and execute tests. Excellent written and verbal communication skills are essential. Interns must be willing to travel occasionally and work well with others in a technical, global environment. Please clearly indicate your interest(s) in your resume, as this is the only way to communicate preferences during the recruiting process. Minimum Qualifications Must be a U.S. citizen Currently enrolled in a bachelor’s degree program in computer engineering, computer science, electrical engineering, or a related field Must be available for 11–14 weeks during Summer 2027 (May–September) Expected graduation date of November 2027 or later 1+ years of experience with programming languages such as C, C++, Java, Python, etc. Preferred Qualifications Candidates actively pursuing a degree with an anticipated graduation between December 2027 and June 2028 Track 1: Embedded Software Experience with real-time embedded software development Experience with cellular systems, including devices and applications for voice and data, and associated test equipment and tools Understanding of communications systems including both physical and upper layers Familiarity with development tools such as Git and Gerrit Familiarity with debugging tools such as JTAG, IDEs, and gdb Experience with digital signal processing Experience with software vulnerability analysis and tools such as IDA Pro Track 2: Software in Test Test automation framework design and development using Python Test design, development, automation, execution, documentation, and debug Experience with cellular systems and associated test equipment and tools Understanding of communications systems including both physical and upper layers Experience evaluating wireless communications systems through drive tests, logging, and post analysis Familiarity with application layer protocols (TCP/IP, UDP, ICMP) and network/socket communications Experience with mobile platform operating systems including Linux, Android, and iOS Familiarity with Linux, Git, Jenkins, Testlink, and Docker Qualcomm’s Internship Program Our interns join world-class teams to help define and build what is next for mobility and the world. jobs.title: Additive Manufacturing Intern Summer 2027
jobs.body: ABOUT ROCKET LAB Rocket Lab is the end-to-end space company building rockets, spacecraft, and critical subsystems that keep the world connected, protected, expand humanity’s reach to the Moon, Mars, and beyond. We move fast, build real hardware for meaningful missions, and make the impossible routine. Come shape the future with us. As an Additive Manufacturing Intern based at Rocket Lab’s site in Long Beach, California, you will have the opportunity to gain an understanding for rocketry and the impact that additive manufacturing has on modern rocket engines. The Additive Manufacturing department provides metal additively manufactured hardware for Electron, Neutron, and Space Systems programs. WHAT YOU’LL GET TO DO As an intern, you will work closely with your mentor and other employees within the department to apply your knowledge and grow your skills both technically and professionally Work with a fast-paced group of professionals to apply engineering and industry concepts to solve real challenges Attend frequent 1:1’s with mentors and supervisors to facilitate success and learning while providing progress updates Enjoy tech talks and network with other interns and employees through social and professional events YOU’LL BRING THESE QUALIFICATIONS Ideal candidates will thrive in ambiguity and are excited to work in small, high-performing teams that are focused on continued learning and growth. Success in this position will be measured by the knowledge and experience you bring to the role, your ability to lead development projects without supervision, and your ability to successfully collaborate across teams to deliver results. Must be enrolled in a bachelor’s, master's or doctorate degree program in an engineering, physics or math discipline and have at least one semester of school remaining post internship GPA of 3.0 or above 3+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) THESE QUALIFICATIONS WOULD BE NICE TO HAVE GPA of 3.5 or above 6+ months of applied engineering experience (internship, laboratory, and personal/team project experience is applicable) Exposure to metal additive manufacturing Strong CAD/CAM modeling skills in Siemens NX, Solidworks, and other CAD/CAM software Finite Element Analysis (FEA) experience Experience with 3D Printing ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS Able to work full-time, on-site for a minimum of 12 consecutive weeks beginning May or June 2027 COMPENSATION AND OTHER BENEFITS Pay Range CA: $28.00 USD Hourly You may be eligible for a stipend to subsidize relocation costs Level and base salary will be determined on a case-by-case basis and may vary based on the following considerations: job-related knowledge and skills, education, and experience. Base salary is just one component of our total rewards package at Rocket Lab. Our comprehensive benefits package includes our industry-leading Employee Stock Purchase Program (with a 15% discount on company stock), top-tier medical plans (HMO, PPO, and a zero cost HDHP option with a significant HSA company contribution), dental and vision coverage, paid vacation and sick time, 11 paid holidays, flexible spending and dependent care accounts, paid parental leave, disability and life insurance, and a 401(k) retirement plan with company match. Additional perks include subsidized EV charging, onsite fitness centers (where available), discounted gym memberships, complimentary snacks and beverages, 50% employee discount on our popular merch store, and a variety of other employee discounts. Eligibility for benefits may vary based on employment status, please check with your recruiter for a comprehensive list of the benefits available for this role. Benefit programs are subject to change at the company’s discretion. Hourly Pay Range (CA Only) $28 — $28 USD WHAT TO EXPECT We’re on a mission to unlock the potential of space to improve life on Earth, but that’s not an easy task. It takes hard work, determination, relentless innovation, teamwork, grit, and an unwavering commitment to achieving what others often deem impossible. Our people out-think, out-work, and out-pace. We pride ourselves on having each other’s backs, checking our egos at the door, and rolling up our sleeves on all tasks big and small. jobs.title: Summer 2027 Internship - Process Engineer - Florida
jobs.body: Work Flexibility: Onsite What You Get Out of the Internship ​​ At Stryker, we believe that developing the next generation of talent is just as important as developing life-changing medical technologies. As an intern, you won’t just observe — you’ll contribute to meaningful projects, gain exposure to leaders who will mentor you, and experience a culture of innovation and teamwork that is shaping the future of healthcare. As an intern, you will : ​ ​ Apply classroom knowledge and gain experience in a fast-paced and growing industry setting ​ Implement new ideas , be constantly challenged, and develop your skills ​ Network with key/high-level stakeholders and leaders of the business ​ Be a part of an innovative team and culture ​ Experience documenting complex processes and presenting them in a clear format Who we want ​​ Challengers. People who seek out the hard projects and work to find just the right solutions. ​ Teammates. Partners who listen to ideas, share thoughts and work together to move the business forward. ​ Charismatic networkers. Relationship-savvy people who intentionally make connections with both internal partners and external contacts. ​ Strategic thinkers. Interns who propose innovative ideas and consistently exceed their performance objectives . ​ Customer-oriented achievers. Individuals with an unparalleled work ethic and customer-focused attitude who bring value to their partnerships. ​ Game changers. Persistent interns who will stop at nothing to live out Stryker’s mission to make healthcare better. Opportunities Available ​ ​ As an Engineering intern at Stryker, you may be placed in one of the following areas, where you will collaborate with cross-functional teams to support product design, quality, testing, software, and manufacturing : ​ ​ ​ Quality : Support initiatives that ensure products meet the highest standards for safety, reliability, and compliance. Projects may include new product development (risk management, design verification/validation, reliability testing), supplier quality, process optimization, and post-market quality improvement . Research & Development (R&D) : Contribute to innovation and product improvement . Design & Development: Research new technologies and customer needs; use tools such as CAD, FEA, LabView, simulations, and software development to design new products or enhance existing ones. Product Engineering: Apply engineering skills to improve the safety, reliability, and performance of current products through analysis, testing, and design improvements. Test Lab: Partner with engineers to evaluate prototypes and verify designs through fixture development, simulated use testing, and quantitative verification of technical specifications. . Manufacturing : Collaborate with design and operations teams to bring products to market efficiently. Projects may include fixture development, assembly line optimization, lean manufacturing implementation, ergonomics/safety improvements, and process validation . Software : Work with engineering teams to design, develop, and test software solutions that integrate with Stryker’s medical technologies. Projects may include embedded systems, automation tools, data analysis, or user-interface improvements that enhance product performance and usability Majors Targeted: Biomedical Engineering , Mechanical Engineering , Electrical Engineering , Software Engineering / Computer Engineering , Manufacturing Engineering , Industrial Engineering , Quality Engineering , Systems Engineering , Related Engineering disciplines What You Need ​​ Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Industrial Engineering, Process Engineering, or a related field and must remain enrolled in a degree-seeking program after the internship. Cumulative 3.0 GPA or above (verified at time of hire) Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S. and not require sponsorship now or in the future . ​ Strong written and verbal communication skills, with proven ability to collaborate and build relationships Demonstrated leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and eagerness to learn in a dynamic environment . $ 20 min hourly wage – $3 5 max hourly wage, sign-on bonus, 11 paid holidays annually, and either paid corporate housing or a living stipend, dependent upon hiring location Travel Percentage: None Stryker Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.body: ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD. At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. jobs.title: 2027 Digital Systems Engineering Graduate Intern
jobs.body: The Aerospace Corporation is the trusted partner to the nation’s space programs, solving the hardest problems and providing unmatched technical expertise. As the operator of a federally funded research and development center (FFRDC), we are broadly engaged across all aspects of space— delivering innovative solutions that span satellite, launch, ground, and cyber systems for defense, civil and commercial customers. When you join our team, you’ll be part of a special collection of problem solvers, thought leaders, and innovators. Join us and take your place in space. The Systems Engineering Division (SED) offers unparalleled expertise in systems engineering to the U.S. government and various public and private agencies, universities, nonprofit organizations, consortia, and commercial companies involved in the advanced development and application of space systems. From systems CONOPs and architecture development to system design and analysis, mission assurance, cost and schedule assessment, and economic market analysis, SED leverages a vast array of engineering and business disciplines across a diverse and dynamic portfolio of space programs and national challenges spanning the total space system lifecycle.” The Digital Systems Engineering Department (DSED ), part of SED, leads the charge in advancing the application of digital system models, digital threads and digital twin capabilities throughout the systems engineering lifecycle. Our work in Digital Engineering (DE) and Model Based Systems Engineering (MBSE) encompasses research, prototyping, development, independent assessments, training, and guidance to help our customers realize complex space and defense systems . The selected candidate will be required to work full-time on-site at our facility in El Segundo, CA or Chantilly, VA. What You’ll be Doing We are seeking a passionate and dedicated Graduate Summer Intern to join our team. This internship offers a hands-on opportunity to develop, simulate, and analyze digital system models for space, ground, and launch architectures with a focus on MBSE methods, tools, and modeling language standards. As part of the DSED team, you will contribute to innovative and challenging projects that shape the future of digital systems engineering. System Architecture and Design: Build, validate, and simulate digital system models representing complex space and defense system architectures and design solutions. System Analysis: Develop complex queries and AI applications that interrogate digital system models for specific information, answering stakeholder questions. Digital Thread Implementation: Assist with federating digital system models with other digital engineering models (mechanical, structural, electrical, software), yielding end-to-end digital thread models. Digital Twin Realization: Develop virtual twin system models that interact with the corresponding physical twin through live telemetry updates. What Corporate Skills You’ll Bring Strong written and oral communication skills Must work well in a team environment Possess organizational, time management and project management skills Demonstrate flexibility and ability to adapt to changing organizational need Interpersonal skills to coordinate efforts and work with other internal and external organizations What You Need to be Successful Currently enrolled full-time in an accredited college/university program, pursuing an M.S. or Ph.D. in Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or a related discipline OR BS degree completed by internship start date and enrolled in a graduate STEM degree program beginning Fall 2027 . Availability to work full-time for a minimum of 10 weeks outside of university term and ability to return to a ( Master's/Phd) degree program full-time after completion of the internship. Minimum GPA of 3.0. Foundational knowledge and some hands-on experience with simulation and analysis tools (e.g., Cameo Simulation Toolkit, MATLAB, Simulink, SimEvents, ModelCenter). A willingness to learn additional tools and languages is essential. Familiarity with descriptive modeling languages (e.g., UML, SysML v1/SysML v2, UAFML) and modeling tools (e.g., Cameo Systems Modeler, Sparx Enterprise Architect, or Rhapsody). Understanding of modeling methodologies such as OOSEM, MagicGrid, or SysMod is a plus. This position requires ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance, which is issued by the United States government. U.S. citizenship is required to obtain a security clearance. Transcripts required How You Can Stand Out It would be impressive if you have one or more of these: Minimum 3.3 GPA. Experience with scripting or programming languages such as python, groovy, Java, or C++. Experience with modeling languages and tools including one or more of the following: SysML, Cameo, Simulink, MATLAB, or similar. Knowledge of systems engineering lifecycle activities, including concept development, requirements definition, architecture, engineering design and analysis, and integration, verification and validation. Familiarity with Digital Engineering concepts (e.g., Digital Ecosystem, Digital Thread, and Digital Twin) and tools such as Syndeia, Teamcenter, Windchill, CREO, or Solidworks. OMG SysML or INCOSE ASEP certification. Strong, demonstrated personal initiative. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, adapt quickly to changing priorities, and balance projects with conflicting time demands. Temporary housing assistance is not available. We offer a competitive compensation package where you’ll be rewarded based on your performance and recognized for the value you bring to our business. The grade-based pay range for this job is listed below. Individual salaries within that range are determined through a wide variety of factors including but not limited to education, experience, knowledge and skills. (Min - Max) $32.00 - $48.00 Pay Basis: Hourly Leadership Competencies Our leadership philosophy is simple: every employee, regardless of level and role, can demonstrate leadership. At Aerospace, our commitment is our people. To cultivate our talent and ensure that we have a strong pipeline of future leaders, we want individuals who: Operate Strategically Lead Change Engage with Impact Foster Innovation Deliver Results Ways We Reward Our Employees During your interview process, our team will provide details of our industry-leading benefits. This core belief empowers us to do our best work at The Aerospace Corporation. Equal Opportunity Commitment The Aerospace Corporation is an equal opportunity employer. jobs.body: Company Overview Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. This goal will be accomplished through the commercialization of the fluoride-salt-cooled, high-temperature reactor (FHR) that can be deployed with robust safety, affordable costs, and flexible operation to accommodate the expansion of variable renewables. Please note: This is a pipeline posting for anticipated Summer 2027 internship opportunities. Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis as internship positions are approved and hiring needs are identified. Job Summary Kairos Power is offering an exciting opportunity for students to join our Civil Structures team as an intern for Summer 2027. This internship provides a unique, hands-on experience supporting the design, analysis, and development of advanced reactor structures while contributing to groundbreaking projects in the nuclear energy sector. Interns will gain practical experience through engineering analysis, high-performance computing, structural design, and experimental investigative methods while working alongside experienced engineers on first-of-a-kind technologies. General Responsibilities Learn and apply applicable building codes, structural design codes, and engineering standards in support of civil and structural engineering projects. Perform engineering calculations and structural analyses using hand calculations and commercially available finite element analysis software such as ANSYS. Evaluate structural designs under static, dynamic, blast, vibration, thermal, and fatigue loading conditions. Develop and maintain 3D models and 2D engineering drawings using CAD software. Prepare engineering reports, technical documentation, calculations, and presentations supporting design and analysis activities. Assist in the evaluation and selection of structural materials and contribute to the development of structural component specifications. Participate in design reviews and multidisciplinary engineering discussions to ensure designs meet safety, quality, operability, and performance objectives. Collaborate with engineers across multiple disciplines to support design development, testing, and continuous improvement initiatives. Participate in training, mentorship, and learning opportunities to strengthen technical and professional development. Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications Current student pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in Civil Engineering or a related field. Demonstrated application of technical skills outside of the classroom through laboratory work, research, extracurricular projects, personal projects, or prior internship/work experience is highly preferred. Experience with CAD software; SolidWorks experience is preferred. Experience with explicit dynamics analysis is a plus. Experience with scripting languages such as Python or Excel Macros is a plus. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications (Outlook, Excel, Word, PowerPoint, etc.). Self-starter with strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills. Proven team player with excellent verbal, written communication/presentation, and interpersonal skills Ability to work with highly collaborative team Ability to solve problems quickly and efficiently Prioritizes and ensures safety of oneself and others Ability to proactively collect, manage and transfer knowledge Ability to seek different and novel ways to create efficiencies when working on problems, challenges and issues Knowledge, Skills & Abilities Working knowledge of civil and structural engineering principles acquired through academic coursework, laboratory experience, research projects, or prior internship experience. Understanding of structural mechanics, statics, mechanics of materials, and engineering analysis fundamentals. Ability to perform engineering calculations and apply analytical thinking to solve technical problems with guidance from experienced engineers. Familiarity with structural analysis methods and finite element analysis (FEA) concepts; experience with engineering software such as ANSYS or similar tools is desirable. Ability to interpret engineering drawings, design calculations, technical specifications, and applicable engineering standards. Basic understanding of engineering design considerations including structural loading, fatigue, vibration, thermal stresses, and material behavior. Familiarity with CAD software and the ability to develop or modify 2D drawings and 3D models. Ability to organize, analyze, and communicate technical information through reports, presentations, and engineering documentation. Strong attention to detail with the ability to produce accurate, organized, and high-quality engineering work. Effective verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills with the ability to collaborate within multidisciplinary engineering teams. Demonstrated initiative, curiosity, and willingness to learn new engineering concepts, software tools, and design methodologies. Strong organizational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple assignments and meet project deadlines. Ability to adapt to changing priorities in a fast-paced engineering and research environment. Commitment to safety, integrity, continuous learning, and professional development. Ability to proactively document, organize, and share technical knowledge with teammates and mentors. Physical Conditions Remaining in a stationary position, often standing, or sitting for prolonged periods Communicating with others to exchange information Environmental Conditions General office environment Accessing the accuracy, neatness and thoroughness of the work assigned High-concentration, demanding and fast-paced Safety and PPE Reading and interpreting hazardous warning signs Wearing proper PPE, to include face mask, face shields, gloves, safety shoes The hourly range for this position is $31-33 for employees working onsite at our Alameda, CA headquarters. Factors that may be used to determine your actual salary may include your education, experience, knowledge, skills, abilities, the market data for your work location, and a comparison to other employees already in the role. jobs.title: System Test Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.location: Delaware, OH, United States; Huntsville, AL, United States
jobs.body: System Test Intern (Summer 2027) Position Summary We are seeking a dedicated and proactive individual to join our Core Engineering team as a System Test Engineering Intern. This internship offers an excellent opportunity to gain hands-on experience in system-level verification and validation of intelligent monitoring and power management products. The ideal candidate is passionate about quality engineering, enjoys methodical problem-solving across hardware and software interfaces, and is eager to apply Generative AI tools to engineering workflows. Responsibilities Execute system-level test cases against firmware builds on physical and virtualized test environments, verifying product behavior across network management protocols (Redfish, SNMP, Modbus, BACnet). Document and report defects with clear reproduction steps, expected vs. actual results, and supporting logs or captures. Participate in defect triage and test review sessions using Agile Development practices. Validate product features including web UI, CLI, and API interfaces on intelligent power and monitoring hardware (PDUs, BMCs, environmental sensors). Use Generative AI tools to support test documentation, log analysis, and workflow automation. Monitor test results for data quality and integrity, identifying discrepancies and collaborating with the team to resolve them. Stay current with trends in test engineering and quality assurance, continuously seeking opportunities to enhance your skills and apply new techniques. Qualifications Must be pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Demonstrated work ethic and detail-orientation. Strong analytical and critical thinking skills. Ability and willingness to learn in a fast-paced environment and produce high-quality work. Collaboration and teamwork. Familiarity with networking fundamentals (IP addressing, HTTP/HTTPS, SSH) is a plus. Exposure to Linux command-line environments is a plus. Physical & Environmental Demands None Time Travel Required None #LI-RB1

jobs.body: Job Details: Job Description: What if your next project helped power the future of technology? At Intel, you'll do more than learn, you'll contribute. From advanced semiconductor manufacturing to AI-powered innovations, you'll play a role in technologies that redefine how the world works, learns, and connects. Unlike many companies where hardware, software, and manufacturing operate separately, Intel brings them together, giving you exposure to everything from research and design to advanced semiconductor manufacturing and global deployment. Bring your curiosity, make an impact, and see where your ideas can take you at Intel. Develop and optimize semiconductor manufacturing processes. Analyze data to improve yield, quality, reliability, and factory performance. Work with advanced semiconductor equipment and fabrication technologies. Apply statistics, data analytics, and failure analysis to solve engineering challenges. Support process control, quality assurance, and continuous improvement initiatives. Contribute to safe, sustainable, and high-performing manufacturing operations. jobs.title: Manufacturing Engineer Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: HydraForce, a Bosch Rexroth company, offers one of the most comprehensive lines of high-quality hydraulic cartridge valves for the mobile and industrial equipment markets. We design and manufacture high performance valves that meet virtually any need encountered in machine design. HydraForce cartridge valves are designed to fit a wide range of industry-common valve cavities. Our employees enjoy a fast-paced and challenging work environment that provides them with daily opportunities to Power Forward their careers. Through interaction with our global network of employees and customers, our employees provide products and solutions that have a global impact. For almost 35 years, HydraForce has been producing the most innovative electro-hydraulic control solutions for the mobile machinery and industrial equipment markets. Throughout the world, you can find our products in a broad range of applications: Agricultural and Turf Care Machinery Construction and Road-Building Equipment Material Handling and Personnel-Lift Equipment Transmission, Engine and Powertrain Controls Forestry and Resource Management Equipment Refuse and Waste Handling Equipment Injection Molding and Press Machinery Other Specialized Mobile and Industrial Applications We are hiring for 2027 Summer Interns! The goal of HydraForce’s internship program is to develop future engineering resources for our organization while providing support to our Engineering groups. We structure the engineering internship to allow candidates the opportunity to develop knowledge and skill-sets unique to our industry. Project tasks reflect an increasing level of technical complexity based on demonstrated proficiency and success on prior assignments. Although there is no guarantee of employment, it is our goal to have our interns fully capable of stepping into an entry-level engineering position upon graduation. Supporting Job Elements: Tool design Creo background (3D modeling) Dimensioning drawings Testing experiments Follow a measurement plan FMEA Improve layouts of assembly cell Developing improvements that will help with throughput Determine methods to eliminate waste Implementing 5S methodology Production assembly assistance Testing assistance Internship Dates: June 2, 2027-August 6, 2027 Committed to an engineering college undergraduate program A minimum on 3.0 GPA Basic proficiency in CAD modeling, preferably in PTC Creo Basic proficiency in MS Office Suite Good written and oral communication and interpersonal skills Self-directed and motivated Majors Desired: Manufacturing, Mechanical, Electrical, Industrial or Mechanical Engineering Technology The US base hourly range for this position will be in between $20- $27 depending on the credits accumulated for the undergraduate students. Your Recruiter can share more details about the specific hourly range during the interview process. Indefinite U.S. work authorized individuals only. Future sponsorship for work authorization unavailable. By choice, we are committed to a diverse workforce and are an equal opportunity employer. Bosch Rexroth welcomes and encourages applications from people with disabilities. Accommodations are available on request for candidates taking part in the selection process. BOSCH is a proud supporter of STEM (Science, Technology, Engineering & Mathematics) Initiatives FIRST Robotics (For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology) AWIM (A World In Motion)

jobs.title: Computer Vision / Applied AI Intern — Summer 2027
jobs.body: Simbe is building the AI-powered operating system for physical retail. Our autonomous robots and multimodal computer vision platform turn complex, constantly changing stores into accurate, actionable intelligence for leading retailers around the world. Simbe combines robotics, computer vision, machine learning, data infrastructure, and customer-focused product design to help retailers improve shelf availability, price and promo execution, inventory accuracy, and store team productivity. Simbe is looking for a Computer Vision / Applied AI Intern to join the team building and improving the computer vision systems that transform imagery collected by Tally into actionable retail intelligence. This internship is designed for students who want hands-on experience applying computer vision and machine learning to real-world data and production systems at meaningful scale.

jobs.title: Sustaining Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Position Summary The Sustaining Engineering Intern will support the Busbar Sustaining Engineering team in maintaining and improving released products throughout their lifecycle. Unlike new product development roles, this position focuses on solving real-world manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and product support challenges affecting existing products. The intern will work closely with sustaining engineers, manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and product engineering teams to investigate production issues, support engineering changes, improve product documentation, analyze recurring problems, and assist with continuous improvement initiatives. This role provides hands-on exposure to engineering problem solving in an engineered-to-order (ETO) manufacturing environment and offers opportunities to contribute to product reliability, quality, manufacturability, and operational excellence. Key Responsibilities Production & Manufacturing Support Assist sustaining engineers in investigating manufacturing and production-related issues. Support resolution of drawing discrepancies, BOM errors, and configuration issues. Participate in shop floor observations and data collection activities. Work with manufacturing teams to understand fabrication, assembly, and quality challenges. Help document and track recurring issues that impact production efficiency. Engineering Change Management Support Engineering Change Orders (ECOs) and Engineering Change Requests (ECRs). Assist with updating drawings, specifications, and Bills of Materials (BOMs). Verify engineering documentation for accuracy and completeness. Help maintain engineering records within PLM and ERP systems. Root Cause Analysis & Quality Improvement Participate in structured problem-solving activities related to product and manufacturing issues. Assist in collecting and analyzing data to identify root causes. Support corrective and preventive action initiatives. Help track implementation and effectiveness of improvement actions. Continuous Improvement & Cost Reduction Support Value Analysis / Value Engineering (VAVE) initiatives. Research opportunities to improve product quality, reduce cost, or simplify manufacturing processes. Assist with standardization and process improvement projects. Analyze engineering and operational data to identify trends and improvement opportunities. Cross-Functional Collaboration Work with manufacturing, quality, supply chain, and engineering teams to support business objectives. Participate in engineering reviews and project meetings. Assist with technical documentation and engineering reports. Communicate findings and recommendations to team members and stakeholders. Internship Project Complete a structured internship project focused on product improvement, manufacturing support, quality enhancement, or process optimization. Present project results, recommendations, and lessons learned to engineering leadership at the conclusion of the internship. Qualifications Required Currently pursuing a Bachelor's degree in: Mechanical Engineering Mechanical Engineering Technology Manufacturing Engineering Industrial Engineering Related Engineering Discipline Completed sophomore year or higher. Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities. Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, Word, and PowerPoint. Strong written and verbal communication skills. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team environment. Preferred Exposure to manufacturing processes and engineering drawings. Familiarity with SolidWorks or similar CAD software. Coursework in: Manufacturing Processes Quality Engineering Materials Mechanical Design Knowledge of Lean Manufacturing or Continuous Improvement concepts. Previous engineering project, internship, robotics, Formula SAE, or manufacturing experience. Learning Opportunities Interns will gain exposure to: Engineering Change Management Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) ERP and BOM Management Root Cause Analysis Quality Systems and Corrective Actions Manufacturing Operations Product Reliability Improvement VAVE and Cost Reduction Cross-Functional Engineering Support Busbar Product Manufacturing and Design Processes Success Measures Successful interns will: Contribute to the resolution of active sustaining engineering issues. Demonstrate effective analytical and problem-solving skills. Support implementation of engineering changes and documentation updates. Deliver measurable improvements in quality, manufacturability, cost, or process efficiency. Successfully complete and present a sustaining engineering project with clear business impact. #LI-RB

jobs.title: Controls Engineer Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: About Zipline Zipline is the world’s largest and most experienced drone delivery service. We are on a mission to serve all humans equally by ensuring access to food, medicine and essential goods anytime, anywhere. We design, build, and operate the world’s largest autonomous logistics system, delivering critical supplies quickly and reliably. Today, Zipline operates on four continents, makes a delivery somewhere in the world every 30 seconds, and has completed millions of deliveries to date, including blood, vaccines, medical supplies, food, and retail products. Our customers include the world’s largest and most prominent healthcare systems, governments, retailers, restaurants and global businesses who rely on us to save lives, reduce emissions, increase economic opportunity, and provide delivery from point A to point B as fast as possible. The drone is only 15% of what we’ve built to enable seamless, reliable, global operations. Our system strengthens supply chains, reduces congestion, and gives people time back. With more than 140 million commercial autonomous miles safely flown, Zipline is redefining access to healthcare, consumer products, and food across the globe. We operate at a global scale and are looking for practical problem solvers who thrive on real-world challenges and rapid growth. Our team is motivated by building systems that have a direct, meaningful impact on people’s lives and by scaling the future of logistics. We are seeking people who sculpt from first principles, enjoy facing adversity, and can do the impossible at record breaking speeds. About the Flight Controls Team Our Flight Controls team is at the heart of Zipline’s product success - we are responsible for developing, testing and maintaining some of the critical flight software systems that enable our aircraft to complete missions autonomously, from takeoff through to predicting and executing a successful delivery, through to landing safely and accurately. We develop novel solutions to give us the responsiveness, robustness and quality we need to ensure our delivery platforms can function in a wide range of increasingly challenging conditions and truly serve everyone in the world equally. The Role Zipline’s people thrive on finding elegant solutions to complex problems, given what exists today and what we can develop to maturity quickly and confidently. We stay close to our customers, learn what really works, and find where we can put the leverage to make a big difference for them now. As an intern on the Flight Controls team, you will learn how we fly autonomous aircraft in a range of challenging flight conditions. Using data from flight testing and simulation as well as our global fleet of customer aircraft, you will be looking for insights that can help improve our design. Through this you’ll have the opportunity to make changes to our systems that will measurably improve our product - your work will not just be theoretical; you will have the opportunity to see your contributions fly! What You'll Do Contribute to the design, implementation, testing and release of innovative flight algorithms that improve the operational performance of our vehicle controllers Create tools and tests to demonstrate your design performance and protect against software regressions, using both theoretical guarantees and simulations Develop and improve simulation and other controls analysis tools so we can predict vehicle performance ahead of time and prove safety and reliability Analyze flight data to assess recent changes and upgrades, looking for regressions and potential areas for future improvement Design onboard integrity tests to communicate when the system performance is degraded Present key results and changes to the broader engineering team What You'll Bring Your applied math skills stand out even among aerospace engineers. You think simulations and working with hardware are both fun. You have owned and developed controls solutions for a team project, thesis, or competition Exposure in one or more of the following areas: precision integrated inertial navigation, dynamic modeling of complex systems, linear control analysis, or optimal control with uncertainty. Software engineering skills, preferably with both embedded software (C, C++, Rust) and technical computing (MATLAB, python, Julia, etc.). Experience with Github and working in a multi-developer environment is an advantage. What Else You Should Know Our internships are full-time positions, in-person at our South San Francisco or Dallas office. We will host our Summer 2027 interns from May/June to August/September. Candidates are limited to three (3) applications within a 30-day period. The hourly rate for this internship is $40 per hour. Additional benefits may include relocation support, a housing stipend, overtime pay, paid sick time, and other benefits, where applicable and subject to local requirements Zipline is an equal opportunity employer and prohibits discrimination and harassment of any type without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, national origin, disability status, genetics, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state or local laws or our own sensibilities. We value diversity at Zipline and welcome applications from those who are traditionally underrepresented in tech. If you like the sound of this position but are not sure if you are the perfect fit, please apply! Zipline is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations to individuals with disabilities. Please let your point of contact at Zipline know if you require any accommodations throughout your interview process. Voluntary Self-Identification For government reporting purposes, we ask candidates to respond to the below self-identification survey. Completion of the form is entirely voluntary. Whatever your decision, it will not be considered in the hiring process or thereafter. Any information that you do provide will be recorded and maintained in a confidential file. As set forth in Zipline ’s Equal Employment Opportunity policy, we do not discriminate on the basis of any protected group status under any applicable law.

jobs.title: Thermal Intern (Summer 2027)
jobs.body: Astranis builds advanced satellites for high orbits, expanding humanity’s reach into the solar system. Today Astranis satellites provide dedicated, secure networks to highly-sophisticated customers across the globe – large enterprises, sovereign governments, and the US military. With five satellites on orbit and many more set to launch soon, the company is servicing a backlog of more than $1 billion of commercial contracts. Astranis is the preferred satellite communications partner for buyers with stringent requirements for uptime, data security, network visibility, and customization. Astranis has raised over $1.2 billion from some of the world’s best investors, including Andreessen Horowitz, Baillie Gifford, Blackrock, Fidelity, Franklin Templeton, and Snowpoint, and employs a team of 500 engineers and entrepreneurs. Astranis designs, builds, and operates its satellites out of its 153,000 sq. ft. headquarters in Northern California, USA. Thermal Intern (Summer 2027) Internships at Astranis typically last for twelve weeks, and are hourly roles designed for students who are currently enrolled at a four-year university. As an Intern, you will have an amazing opportunity to work on hard problems — we pride ourselves on giving everyone at Astranis a chance to do meaningful work on complex projects, no matter their seniority. Many past interns have designed and tested hardware/software that is heading to space on our first satellite, and many of them are now full-time employees at Astranis. If you have already graduated from a four-year university, please apply to be an Associate Engineer. Role Work together with the engineering team to design, evaluate, build, and test satellite hardware and/or software. Support design trades that successfully balance performance margins, resource use, risk, cost, and schedule. Perform thermal analysis to varying degrees of fidelity (simplified to detailed) on a variety of different types of hardware such as propulsion components, batteries, high powered electronics, RF components, mechanisms, and printed circuit boards (PCBs). Design, evaluate, procure and test thermal solutions such as heaters, heat pipes, thermal interface materials, and surface coatings. Develop processes and procedures for integration and assembly which ensure thermal design intent is met. Collaborate with the integration and test team in the installation of thermal hardware as needed. Plan and run thermal vacuum testing and verification at the component and spacecraft level. Requirements Currently pursuing a B.S. or M.S. in mechanical, aerospace, or equivalent technical degree (e.g. physics or applied math) A passion and enthusiasm for hardware development, including working in a fast-paced environment and hands-on design and development Demonstrated ability to personally design, build, and test hardware from scratch. US Citizenship or Green Card Don't meet them all? Not a problem. Please apply even if you do not meet all these criteria. Bonus Experience with CAD Experience with analytical software thermal analysis such as ANSYS and Thermal Desktop Experience with electronics systems design and packaging Experience (projects or previous internships) related to aerospace The base pay for this position is $29.00 per hour. Base Hourly Pay $29 — $29 USD U.S. Citizenship, Lawful Permanent Residency, or Refugee/Asylee Status Required (To comply with U.S. Government space technology export regulations, applicant must be a U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident of the United States, or other protected individual as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3)) Our mission and products are built for everyone, regardless of gender, race, creed, or background. We believe in a diverse and inclusive workplace, and we invite all people to join our team and bring their unique perspectives to make us stronger. jobs.title: Mechanical Engineer Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: Astronics Advanced Electrical Systems (AES) is seeking a highly motivated Mechanical Engineering Intern – Summer 2027 to join our dynamic and high-performing Mechanical Engineering Team at our Kirkland, WA facility. This is a full-time, on-site internship position. Candidates local to the greater Seattle/Kirkland, WA area are strongly preferred, as relocation support is not available for this role. Our paid summer internship offers students the unique opportunity to gain hands-on experience in the aerospace industry while working alongside some of the brightest minds in mechanical and electrical engineering. As a vital member of our Cabin Electronics Product Group, you will contribute to the development of innovative new in-seat power systems for the commercial airline industry. The group’s EmPower® product line provides a variety of scalable power solutions for aircraft passenger cabins and flight decks. Our systems are used by over 280 airlines, IFE suppliers, and all major aircraft OEM manufacturers worldwide. Position Summary We’re seeking creative, driven, and detail-oriented individuals who are eager to put their engineering education into action. As a Mechanical Engineering Intern , you will apply engineering principles to design, evaluate, and support the development of cutting-edge products within the aerospace sector. Under the guidance and mentorship of our experienced engineering staff, you will engage in design, testing, and research activities, while significantly contributing to impactful, real-world projects. Potential areas of focus include product development and design, product support, and research and testing. Key Responsibilities As a Mechanical Engineering Intern at AES, you will: Develop and prototype design solutions, leveraging in-house resources such as 3D printing and a benchtop CNC machine . Conduct tests to evaluate hardware solutions and performance characteristics in support of design objectives. Design product components or hardware using detailed concept descriptions provided by the engineering team. Explore and utilize advanced engineering tools, including SolidWorks , SolidWorks Flow Simulation , and ANSYS . Build hands-on lab skills through activities such as hardware assembly , environmental testing , and fit checks . Minimum Qualifications Education/Experience: Currently enrolled in an accredited college/university program with at least three years of coursework completed by the start of Summer 2027. Pursuing a degree in Mechanical Engineering or a related discipline, with an emphasis on thermal-related computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and/or vibrational dynamics preferred. Experience designing printed circuit boards and cooling techniques for electronic equipment preferred. Skills, Competencies, and Attributes: Strong attention to detail with excellent organizational skills. Ability to manage multiple tasks effectively and prioritize workload. Demonstrated problem-solving skills with an aptitude for processing complex inputs and applying logical reasoning. Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote). Clear and efficient written and verbal communication skills. Proactive and self-motivated with the ability to work autonomously, yet willing to collaborate and seek guidance from senior technical staff as needed. Employment Eligibility Requirements U.S. Person Status: As a U.S. Department of Defense contractor, AES must comply with International Traffic in Arms Regulations (ITAR). Candidates must meet the definition of a U.S. Person to be eligible (U.S. Citizen, U.S. National, or U.S. Permanent Resident). Successful completion of a pre-employment background check and drug screening (inclusive of cannabis) is required. Internship Compensation This is a paid internship with a competitive hourly rate of $28.00–$30.00 , depending on experience and qualifications. The position is eligible for holiday pay. At Astronics Advanced Electrical Systems , we celebrate innovation, foster collaboration, and are dedicated to shaping the future of aviation. Join us this summer and be part of our mission to lead the aerospace industry through groundbreaking electrical power solutions! Interested candidates, please apply today! Astronics Corporation (Nasdaq: ATRO) serves the world's aerospace, defense, and other mission critical industries with proven, innovative technology solutions. Astronics works side-by-side with customers, integrating its array of power, connectivity, lighting, structures, interiors, and test technologies to solve complex challenges. For over 50 years, Astronics has delivered creative, customer-focused solutions with exceptional responsiveness. Today, global airframe manufacturers, airlines, militaries, completion centers and Fortune 500 companies rely on the collaborative spirit and innovation of Astronics. The Company's strategy is to increase its value by developing technologies and capabilities that provide innovative solutions to its targeted markets. For more information on Astronics and its solutions, visit www.Astronics.com . All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected status.

jobs.title: Summer 2027 Intern - Computational Design Intern
jobs.location: Warren, Michigan, United States of America
jobs.body: Job Description 2027 Summer Intern – Computational Design The Role: General Motors Design is seeking a Computational Design Intern to support the development of innovative digital tools, workflows, and automotive design studies within a creative studio environment. This internship offers qualified candidates the opportunity to explore careers at GM while gaining practical experience at the intersection of computational design, digital sculpting, automotive form development, and advanced 3D modeling. The intern will collaborate with Design, Sculpting, and Engineering teams to investigate new ways of generating, evaluating, and refining digital models of future automotive themes. The role provides exposure to aesthetic decision-making, design technology, production methods, program timing, and the materials and processes used in automotive digital development. The Team: The intern will collaborate with GM Design, Sculpting, and Engineering teams in an automotive design studio environment. What You’ll Do: · Collaborate with Design, Sculpting, and Engineering teams to interpret sketches, design intent, and technical requirements. · Develop digital studies, tools, and model variations for future automotive themes using computational design and digital-sculpting techniques. · Explore parametric, procedural, generative, and automation-based approaches to support automotive form development and design iteration. · Build and refine 3D models while maintaining an understanding of proportion, line, surface quality, and visual harmony. · Translate creative concepts into clear digital workflows, prototypes, visualizations, or production-ready modeling studies. · Support the development of reusable scripts, definitions, templates, or processes that improve design exploration and studio efficiency. · Work within established digital modeling standards while helping evaluate emerging technologies and best practices. · Present project progress, design studies, and finished work for Design leadership during midterm and final reviews. · Support general computational design and sculpting assignments within the studio environment. · Document methods, iterations, and results so that workflows can be communicated and reused by the broader team. Your Skills & Abilities (Required Qualifications): · Pursuit of a bachelor’s or advanced degree in Computational Design, Industrial Design, Product Design, Transportation Design, Architecture, Animation, Game Design, Computer Science, Fine Arts, Sculpture, Ceramics, or a related field. · Must be graduating between December 2027 and May 2029. · Able to work full-time, 40 hours per week during the summer months. · Strong interest in the relationship between design, technology, geometry, and 3D form development. · Ability to work collaboratively in a creative, iterative, and feedback-driven studio environment. · Portfolio demonstrating 3D design, computational design, digital modeling, visual development, or related creative work. What will give you a Competitive Edge (Preferred Qualifications): · Experience with computational, parametric, procedural, or generative design workflows. · Experience with software such as Rhino/Grasshopper, Alias, Unigraphics/NX, or comparable 3D platforms. · Programming or scripting experience in Python, C#, or a similar language. · Basic understanding of automotive design and sculpting principles, including proportion, line, surface, volume, and reflection quality. · Experience developing tools, scripts, plug-ins, procedural definitions, or automated modeling workflows. · Understanding of digital sculpting, polygonal modeling, NURBS modeling, subdivision surfaces, or related 3D techniques. · Ability to communicate design intent and technical concepts through sketches, diagrams, models, renderings, or presentations. · Curiosity, initiative, and the ability to learn new software and workflows quickly. jobs.title: Design Verification Intern, MS - Summer 2027
jobs.location: Santa Clara, CA; Austin, TX; Westborough, MA; Boise, ID; Morrisville, NC
jobs.body: About Marvell Marvell’s semiconductor solutions are the essential building blocks of the data infrastructure that connects our world. Across enterprise, cloud and AI, and carrier architectures, our innovative technology is enabling new possibilities. At Marvell, you can affect the arc of individual lives, lift the trajectory of entire industries, and fuel the transformative potential of tomorrow. For those looking to make their mark on purposeful and enduring innovation, above and beyond fleeting trends, Marvell is a place to thrive, learn, and lead. Your Team, Your Impact Marvell’s Design Verification teams span across multiple domains, giving you the opportunity to work on technologies that power next-generation cloud, AI, storage, and networking solutions. Some teams focus on pre-silicon emulation and verification for ODSP-related chips. Other teams focus on ASIC Design, where they testbench with UVM methodology and test specific SOC designs at block/cluster/full chip levels. Other teams focus on powering the full range of network connectivity from the optics of the AI GPU boards to top of the rack optical fibers and active copper cables of the data centers and their fabrics. Across all groups, you’ll collaborate with your direct team and cross-functional partners (across software, physical design, digital design, and more) to deliver robust, scalable solutions that enable Marvell’s leadership in data infrastructure. What You Can Expect Dive deep into the architecture of our cutting-edge processors and learn exactly how they function Use industry-standard tools to create powerful simulation environments that mimic real-world conditions Develop smart, automated tests that push our designs to their limits , creatively trying to "break" the chip to find & troubleshoot hidden flaws & failed simulations Analyze test coverage results & metrics Collaborate with chip architects and designers to solve complex problems and contribute to a team building real products What We're Looking For Currently enrolled in a Master' s Degree in Ele ctrical Engineeri ng , Computer Engineering, or a related field with an expected graduation date between Fall 2027 – Summer 2028 Completed courses focusing on computer architecture, logic, processor, memory system, V erilog , VLSI, VHDL, UVM, analog, integrated circuit design, digital logic design, SoC/ASIC design, verification principles, signals, system and signal processing Proficiency in programming & scripting languages like Python, C, C++, Perl, Java Experience using tool s like Synopsys, Cadence, or Mentor to run simulations and write & debug a testbench Hands-on experience with RTL integration and bring-up system Experience with debugging complex hardware/software interactions Strong analysis, problem solving, and communication skills Expected Base Pay Range (USD) 35 - 70, $ per hour. The successful candidate’s starting base pay will be determined based on job-related skills, experience, qualifications, work location and market conditions. The expected base pay range for this role may be modified based on market conditions. This role is eligible to participate in Marvell's bonus and equity plans, including a new hire equity grant and annual equity refreshers, ensuring you are rewarded for your contributions and remain invested in the company's long-term success. Additional Compensation and Benefit Elements Marvell is committed to providing exceptional, comprehensive benefits that support our employees at every stage - from internship to retirement and through life’s most important moments. Our offerings are built around four key pillars: financial well-being, family support, mental and physical health, and recognition. Highlights for our interns: medical, dental, and vision coverage, perks and discounts, robust mental health resources to prioritize emotional well-being, and paid holidays. Additional compensation may be available for intern PhD candidates. We look forward to sharing more with you during the interview process. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability or protected veteran status. Any applicant who requires a reasonable accommodation during the selection process should contact Marvell HR Helpdesk at TAOps@marvell.com . Interview Integrity To support fair and authentic hiring practices, candidates are not permitted to use AI tools (such as transcription apps, real-time answer generators like ChatGPT or Copilot, or automated note-taking bots) during interviews. These tools must not be used to record, assist with, or enhance responses in any way. Our interviews are designed to evaluate your individual experience, thought process, and communication skills in real time. Use of AI tools without prior instruction from the interviewer will result in disqualification from the hiring process. This position may require access to technology and/or software subject to U.S. export control laws and regulations, including the Export Administration Regulations (EAR). As such, applicants must be eligible to access export-controlled information as defined under applicable law. Marvell may be required to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce and/or the U.S. Department of State. Except for U.S. citizens, lawful permanent residents, or protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3), all applicants may be subject to an export license review process prior to employment. #LI-TT1

jobs.title: Intern - Semiconductor Research & Technology Development
jobs.body: Our vision is to transform how the world uses information to enrich life for all . Micron Technology is a world leader in innovating memory and storage solutions that accelerate the transformation of information into intelligence, inspiring the world to learn, communicate and advance faster than ever. The Innovation, Technology & Products (ITP) organization develops next-generation memory technologies and enables future Micron products. At Albany Nanotech, Micron is expanding its advanced research and development capabilities with a focus on leading-edge lithography, materials innovation, technology pathfinding, and strategic semiconductor ecosystem partnerships. This location plays a critical role in accelerating semiconductor technology development through collaboration with industry leaders, research institutions, and equipment partners. Micron is seeking highly motivated Master's or PhD students to join the Summer 2027 Semiconductor Technology Development Internship Program in Albany, New York. Interns will contribute to advanced semiconductor research projects supporting future memory technologies and process innovations. This internship provides hands-on experience working alongside engineers and researchers in a world-class semiconductor R&D environment. Interns will analyze technical challenges, develop innovative solutions, and present project outcomes to technical leadership at the conclusion of the program. Responsibilities Support semiconductor research and development activities by designing experiments, collecting data, and evaluating results to advance future technology capabilities. Analyze technical and process data using statistical methods to identify trends, solve engineering problems, and develop actionable recommendations. Collaborate with multi-functional engineering teams, researchers, and external partners to execute technology development projects. Document research findings and effectively communicate technical results through reports, presentations, and project evaluations. Leverage AI-enabled tools, advanced analytics platforms, and digital solutions to improve research productivity, accelerate problem-solving, enhance data analysis, and support technical decision-making in accordance with Micron's responsible and secure AI practices. Minimum Qualifications Currently pursuing a Master's or PhD degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science & Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Physics, Chemistry, Computer Engineering, Data Science, or a related STEM field. Expected graduation date of December 2027 or later. Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills through academic research, coursework, or technical projects. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to present technical information effectively. Ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary teams. Preferred Qualifications Experience in semiconductor manufacturing, semiconductor research, laboratory environments, or cleanroom operations. Knowledge of experimental design, statistical analysis, and process characterization techniques. Experience with data analysis tools such as Python, R, MATLAB, JMP, or similar software platforms. Demonstrated research experience through independent projects, technical publications, conference presentations, or equivalent academic achievements. Experience using AI-assisted tools, advanced analytics platforms, or computational methods to improve engineering workflows, research efficiency, data analysis, or technical problem-solving. The US base salary range that Micron Technology estimates it could pay for this full-time position is: $46.51 - $46.51 an hour Additional compensation may include benefits, bonuses and equity. The range displayed on each job posting reflects the minimum and maximum target base pay for new hire salaries of the position across all US locations. Within the range, individual pay is determined by work location and additional job-related factors, including knowledge, skills, experience, tenure and relevant education or training. The pay scale is subject to change depending on business needs. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process. Additionally, Micron benefits include a robust paid time-off program and paid holidays. For additional information regarding the Benefit programs available, please see the Benefits Guide posted on micron.com/careers/benefits . jobs.title: Supplier Quality Intern - Summer 2027
jobs.body: HydraForce, a Bosch Rexroth company, offers one of the most comprehensive lines of high-quality hydraulic cartridge valves for the mobile and industrial equipment markets. We design and manufacture high performance valves that meet virtually any need encountered in machine design. HydraForce cartridge valves are designed to fit a wide range of industry-common valve cavities. Our employees enjoy a fast-paced and challenging work environment that provides them with daily opportunities to Power Forward their careers. Through interaction with our global network of employees and customers, our employees provide products and solutions that have a global impact. For almost 35 years, HydraForce has been producing the most innovative electro-hydraulic control solutions for the mobile machinery and industrial equipment markets. Throughout the world, you can find our products in a broad range of applications: Agricultural and Turf Care Machinery Construction and Road-Building Equipment Material Handling and Personnel-Lift Equipment Transmission, Engine and Powertrain Controls Forestry and Resource Management Equipment Refuse and Waste Handling Equipment Injection Molding and Press Machinery Other Specialized Mobile and Industrial Applications The goal of HydraForce’s internship program is to develop future engineering resources for our organization while providing support to our Supplier Quality Engineering team. We structure the engineering internship to allow candidates the opportunity to develop knowledge and skill-sets unique to our industry. Project tasks reflect an increasing level of technical complexity based on demonstrated proficiency and success on prior assignments. Although there is no guarantee of employment, it is our goal to have our interns fully capable of stepping into an entry-level engineering position upon graduation. Supporting Job Elements: Create Value Stream Maps and then create projects to lean out process Clean, merge and analyze data from multiple data sources Create databases to house past and future data Use tools and techniques from Six Sigma, Lean, to analyze and solve problems Assist in continuous improvement projects Day to day support activities but not limited to inspection, sorting, problem investigations, and PPAP approvals Assist in non-conforming material reports and analysis Create and modify existing systems that track our metrics Create, improve on documentation such as control plans, FMEAs, WI, and process flows Qualifications: Advanced Excel skills; Power Bi, Minitab Committed to an engineering college undergraduate program Completed a minimum of 24 hours at the university level Coursework and/or experience in setting up databases, SPC, data collection Coursework and/or experience in statistical analysis, lean tools Coursework and/or experience in measurement systems Basic experience in 3D modeling; Understanding of GD&T Working knowledge of problem solving techniques and FMEAs Great written and verbal communication and interpersonal skills Majors Desired: Industrial Engineering, Mechanical Engineering Internship Dates: June 2, 2027-August 6, 2027 The US base hourly range for this position will be in between $20- $27 depending on the credits accumulated for the undergraduate students. jobs.body: JOB SUMMARY At S&C Electric Company , a 100% employee-owned company, we help keep the lights on for people and businesses worldwide. Our manufacturing roles build the equipment that protects the critical infrastructure of the power grid, and each of our team members lends their unique skills to this crucial mission. We empower our people by providing pathways to a long-term career and support them in their professional growth by sustaining a culture founded on respect, strengthened by collaboration, and measured by our shared successes. The manufacturing industry is booming with opportunities to learn new things, expand your skills, and build a long-term career. Join S&C to make an impact on tomorrow’s energy challenges and become an employee-owner! Available Shift: 1st shift: 8:00 am – 4:30 pm, Monday – Friday Full-Time Summer 2027 Internship in Franklin, WI At S&C, we are dedicated to providing competitive and equitable compensation for all our team members, and we are committed to transparency in our pay practices. The estimated per hourly range for this position is $22 - 30 per hour based on experience. Competitive Weekly Pay Period The Test Equipment Engineering & Maintenance Intern will be responsible for troubleshooting electronic assemblies and systems, identifying defect trends, finding root causes and maintaining equipment reliability. Must be able to work in a fast-paced environment and have excellent interpersonal skills. The position reports to the Manager - Test Equipment Engineering & Maintenance. Investigate root cause and propose solutions. Enter defects and repair data into asset management database. Perform mechanical assembly and wiring following provided drawings and schematics. Ability to write test software a plus. Configuration of replacement PCs for existing test systems. Implement upgrades or assist in redesigning current test systems. To select this job as one of interest to you, at a minimum, you must have the following: In-progress degree program from an accredited university/college program with a concentration in Electronics Engineering Technology, Electronics Engineering, or related field and returning to school full-time after the work session. Excellent verbal and written communication skills. Ability to work independently in a service-oriented environment. Solid understanding of lab test and measurement instrumentation. Knowledge of analog and digital circuit theory and principles. Computer skills - MS Outlook, Word and Excel. Ability to read and interpret electrical/mechanical drawings. MAJOR PHYSICAL DEMANDS Standing Lifting Able to lift up to 30 lbs. Walking Carrying Pushing Pulling Bending Reaching Handling Other Ready to make an impact and become an employee-owner?
